definition_zh: 素食者；吃素的；素食的
definition_en: a person who does not eat meat or fish, or something that contains no meat or fish
core_image: 一张餐桌上摆满蔬菜、豆类和谷物，没有肉
scene: 朋友聚餐时，她点了一份全素的咖喱，不要任何肉类。She ordered a vegetable curry with no meat because she is a strict vegetarian.
sceneCN: 这里 vegetarian 是「素食者」（第 1 个义项：不吃肉或鱼的人）；句意：她点了一份没有肉的蔬菜咖喱，因为她是严格的素食者。

pos.zh: 素食的；不含肉类的；vegetarian 作此义时也指「（某人）吃素的」

collocations.zh: 乳素食者（吃奶制品但不吃蛋和肉）

derivatives.zh: vegetarian 加 -ism 构成，义为「素食主义」
与本词共享拉丁语词根 vegetare（生长），义为「蔬菜」
由 vegetarian 截短改拼而成（一九四四年），义为「纯素食者」

senses.title: A person who eats no meat
senses.definition: a person who chooses not to eat meat or fish
senses.definitionCN: 选择不吃肉或鱼的人
senses.example: My brother has been a vegetarian for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 我弟弟已经吃素十年了。
senses.why: The word fuses vegetable with the agent ending -ian, so a vegetarian is literally a person of vegetables rather than meat.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把 vegetable 与表示人的后缀 -ian 拼在一起，字面就是「以蔬菜为食的人」，与吃肉相对。

senses.title: Food or a meal without meat
senses.definition: describing food, a dish, or a menu that contains no meat or fish
senses.definitionCN: 形容食物、菜肴或菜单不含肉或鱼
senses.example: The hotel keeps a vegetarian option on every menu.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店每份菜单上都有一道素食可选。
senses.why: Once a person can be vegetarian, the food that suits that person takes the same label.
senses.whyCN: 既然人可以叫 vegetarian，适合这类人吃的食物也顺理成章地获得同一个标签。

senses.title: Relating to a meatless way of life
senses.titleCN: 素食主义的；与吃素相关的
senses.definition: connected with the practice, diet, or movement of not eating meat
senses.definitionCN: 与不吃肉的饮食习惯或生活方式有关的
senses.example: The town opened its first vegetarian society last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇去年春天成立了第一个素食者协会。
senses.why: The label spreads from people and food to institutions such as societies, diets, and publications.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签从人和食物扩展到协会、饮食方式和出版物等制度性事物上。

senses.title: A follower of a plant based faith
senses.definition: a person who avoids meat for religious or ethical reasons
senses.definitionCN: 出于宗教或伦理原因而戒肉的人
senses.example: The monks follow a vegetarian rule in their monastery.
senses.exampleCN: 僧侣们在寺院里遵守素食戒规。
senses.why: Long before modern diets, religious communities ate no meat, so the modern word often covers that older practice.
senses.whyCN: 早在现代饮食风潮之前，宗教团体就戒肉，所以现代这个词也常用来概括那种古老的修行。

intro.en: Vegetarian is an English coinage of the nineteenth century, made from vegetable on the model of words in -arian. It is not from Latin vegetus, although both share the idea of being lively and growing.
intro.cn: vegetarian 是十九世纪英语自造的词，仿照 -arian 类词（如 humanitarian）由 vegetable 构成；它并非直接来自拉丁语 vegetus，只是两者都带有「生长、有生气」的意思。

items.en: Vegetare means to grow or enliven, and vegetus means lively.
items.cn: 动词 vegetare 意为生长、使有生气，形容词 vegetus 意为有活力的。

items.en: Vegetable appears in English first for any growing plant.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语中的 vegetable 初指任何会生长的植物。

items.en: The Vegetarian Society appears in Britain and the term is coined soon after.
items.cn: 十九世纪四十年代英国出现素食者协会，这个词很快被创造出来。

items.en: Vegetarian is formed from vegetable with the ending -arian.
items.cn: vegetarian 由 vegetable 加上 -arian 词尾构成。

items.en: The adjective use spreads to menus, diets, and restaurants.
items.cn: 现代英语中形容词用法扩展到菜单、饮食与餐厅。

note.en: Vegetarian is easily confused with vegetarianism and with vegan, and in meaning it neighbours plant based and meatless.
note.cn: vegetarian 容易与 vegetarianism、vegan 混淆；在意义上它与「植物性饮食」「无肉」一类说法相邻。

entries.definition: the practice of not eating meat
plants in general
entries.definitionCN: 植被；植物（与 vegetarian 同出拉丁语「生长」词根）

entries.definition: a doctor who treats animals
entries.definitionCN: 兽医（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a person who eats no animal products at all
entries.definitionCN: 纯素食者；不食用任何动物制品的人

entries.definition: a person who eats mainly fruit
entries.definitionCN: 果食者；主要以水果为食的人

entries.definition: an animal that feeds on plants

normalIntro.en: Vegetarian is vegetable plus -arian, a person marked by vegetables, so the plate is full of greens and grains instead of meat.
normalIntro.cn: vegetarian 就是 vegetable 加上 -arian，指「以蔬菜为标记的人」，餐盘里满是青菜与谷物，而不见肉。

normal.en: The ending -arian appears in humanitarian and librarian, both naming kinds of people.
normal.cn: 后缀 -arian 见于 humanitarian 与 librarian，都是指某一类人。

normal.en: A strict vegetarian eats no meat and often no fish either.
normal.cn: 严格的素食者不吃肉，通常也不吃鱼。

normal.en: The word vegetable grows from a Latin root meaning to grow, just like vegetation.
normal.cn: vegetable 来自表示「生长」的拉丁语词根，与 vegetation 同源。

normal.en: Vegan was formed from vegetarian by cutting and respelling, but the two words mark different diets.
normal.cn: vegan 由 vegetarian 截短改拼而来，但两者划分的是不同的饮食。

normal.en: Go vegetarian means to change to a meatless diet.
normal.cn: go vegetarian 就是改成吃素的饮食。

abstract.en: Picture a garden plate: tomatoes, beans, and rice, with an empty space where the meat would be.
abstract.cn: 想象一个菜园般的餐盘：番茄、豆子和米饭，原本放肉的位置留着空白。

abstract.en: See a menu with a small green leaf printed beside a few dishes.
abstract.cn: 想象一张菜单上，几道菜旁边印着一片小绿叶。

abstract.en: Imagine a family argument over the dinner table, one plate of meat quietly removed.
abstract.cn: 想象一家人正在餐桌前争论，一盘肉被悄悄端走。

examples.en: Several guests asked for a vegetarian dish at the wedding.
examples.cn: 婚礼上有几位客人要了素食菜。

examples.en: Vegetarians often take extra care to get enough iron and protein.
examples.cn: 素食者常常格外注意摄取足够的铁和蛋白质。

examples.en: The restaurant became fully vegetarian in less than a year.
examples.cn: 这家餐厅不到一年就完全改成了素菜馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维吉塔瑞恩」——把「vegetable」抱满怀的「人」，就是说吃素的人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 vegetable（蔬菜，源于拉丁语「生长」词根）+ -arian（人、信奉者）= vegetarian，核心义「以蔬菜为食的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Vegetarian names the person first, then the food without meat, then the wider diet and movement, and finally older religious abstention.
sensesIntro.cn: vegetarian 先指人，再指不含肉的食物，接着扩展到整套饮食与运动，最后覆盖古老的宗教戒肉传统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate of plants with no meat on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盘只有植物、没有肉的饭菜。

branches.en: The person is named by the food on the plate.
branches.cn: 人由盘中的食物来命名。

branches.en: The food itself takes the label.
branches.cn: 食物本身也获得这个标签。

branches.en: The label spreads to diets, menus, and societies.
branches.cn: 标签扩展到饮食、菜单与协会。

branches.en: Religious abstention from meat predates the modern word.
branches.cn: 宗教戒肉早于这个现代词出现。

branches.en: Both the person and the movement share the same vegetable root.
branches.cn: 人与这种运动共享同一个「蔬菜」词根。

intro.en: Vegetarian is a blended English word: the base vegetable plus the suffix -arian, later adding -ism and inspiring vegan.
intro.cn: vegetarian 是一个英语拼合词：基础词 vegetable 加后缀 -arian，后来又加上 -ism，还催生了 vegan。

latinIntro.en: The deepest layer is Latin vegetare, to grow, which gives vegetable, vegetation, and vegetarian alike.
latinIntro.cn: 最底层是拉丁语 vegetare（生长），vegetable、vegetation 与 vegetarian 都由此而来。

items.example: The root veget- appears in vegetable and vegetation.
items.exampleCN: 词根 veget- 出现在 vegetable 与 vegetation 中。

items.example: Vegetable is the base of the compound.
items.exampleCN: vegetable 是拼合词的基础部分。

items.meaningCN: 表示人或信奉者的后缀
items.example: The suffix -arian forms vegetarian.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -arian 构成 vegetarian。

items.meaningCN: 表示主义或实践的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ism forms vegetarianism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 vegetarianism。

items.meaning: the practice of not eating meat
items.example: Vegetarianism grew quickly in the cities.
items.exampleCN: 素食主义在城市中迅速传播。

items.example: Vegetation shares the growing root.
items.exampleCN: vegetation 共享「生长」词根。

items.meaning: a person who avoids all animal products
items.example: Vegan was cut from vegetarian.
items.exampleCN: vegan 由 vegetarian 截短而来。

items.example: Lacto- builds lacto-vegetarian.
items.exampleCN: 组合形式 lacto- 构成 lacto-vegetarian。

items.example: Ovo- builds ovo-vegetarian.
items.exampleCN: 组合形式 ovo- 构成 ovo-vegetarian。

definition_zh: 激情；强烈；激烈；（言辞、情绪的）猛烈程度
definition_en: the quality of being violent in feeling, or showing very strong, forceful emotion
core_image: 一股热气从上冲的胸腔里冲出，把话连珠炮一样推出去
scene: 会议开到一半，争论双方的语气越来越冲，谁也不肯退让。Her vehemence surprised everyone in the room.
sceneCN: 这里 vehemence 是「激情」（第 1 个义项：强烈而外露的情感力量）；句意：她那股激烈的劲头让屋里的每个人都吃了一惊。

pos.zh: 激情；强烈；激烈；（情感、言辞的）猛烈

derivatives.zh: 由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「激烈的；强烈的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「激烈地；强烈地」
较少见的同义异形，义为「激烈；激情」

senses.title: Strength of visible feeling
senses.definition: the quality of having strong, forceful feeling that others can clearly see
senses.definitionCN: 强烈而外露、别人一眼就能看出的情感力量
senses.example: She spoke about the village with real vehemence.
senses.exampleCN: 她谈起那个村子时语气真的很带劲。
senses.why: Latin vehementia came from vehemens, fiery or carried away, so the first strand of meaning is heat of feeling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vehementia 来自 vehemens（火热的、被情绪带着走的），所以第一层含义就是情感的热度。

senses.title: Forcefulness of speech or action
senses.definition: the forceful energy shown in words, gestures, or an argument
senses.definitionCN: 言语、手势或争论中表现出的那股冲劲
senses.example: The lawyer argued with unexpected vehemence.
senses.exampleCN: 那位律师以出人意料的激烈口吻争辩。
senses.why: The inner heat is pressed out into speech and gesture, so vehemence names the force behind the words.
senses.whyCN: 内心的热度被压进话语和手势里，所以 vehemence 也指话语背后那股力道。

senses.title: Fierceness of a natural force
senses.definition: the violent strength of a storm, wind, fire, or other physical force
senses.definitionCN: 风暴、风、火等自然力量的猛烈程度
senses.example: The gale hit the coast with great vehemence.
senses.exampleCN: 大风以极大的猛烈劲头袭击了海岸。
senses.why: The physical image of something rushing and burning lets the word describe storms and other forces.
senses.whyCN: 那个奔涌燃烧的画面，让这个词也能用来形容风暴等自然力量。

senses.title: Intensity of a denial or attack
senses.definition: the intensity with which someone denies, attacks, or objects to something
senses.definitionCN: 某人否认、抨击或反对某事时的猛烈程度
senses.example: He denied the charge with startling vehemence.
senses.exampleCN: 他以惊人的激烈程度否认了那项指控。
senses.why: When heat of feeling is aimed at a person or claim, it becomes defence or attack, often with suspicion attached.
senses.whyCN: 当情感的热度对准某个人或某个说法，它就成了辩解或攻击，而猛烈的否认也常让人起疑。

senses.title: Passionate commitment to a cause
senses.definition: an ardent, wholehearted devotion to a belief, cause, or person
senses.definitionCN: 对信念、事业或某个人全心全意的热忱投入
senses.example: She defended the reform with lifelong vehemence.
senses.exampleCN: 她以一生的热忱为自己的改革主张辩护。
senses.why: The same inward fire, turned toward a mistaken belief, becomes the religious sense of fiery zeal.
senses.whyCN: 同一股内燃的火，转向某个信念时，就成了宗教意味上的狂热热忱。

intro.en: Vehemence comes from Latin vehementia, the noun of vehemens, fiery or carried away. The older form was vehemens beside the verb vehere, and the exact link is generally explained as a scribal confusion, though the details remain open.
intro.cn: vehemence 来自拉丁语 vehementia，是 vehemens（火热的、被带着走的）的名词。较早的形式与动词 vehere 有关，一般认为中间发生了书写混淆，但细节仍有争议。

items.en: Vehemens describes something violent, fiery, or lacking restraint.
items.cn: vehemens 形容猛烈、火热或缺乏节制的事物。

items.en: Vehementia is the quality of being violent or fiery.
items.cn: vehementia 是猛烈、热烈的性质名词。

items.en: Vehementia is extended to eagerness and zealous fervour.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中，vehementia 扩展到热切与宗教狂热。

items.en: Vehemence enters English and covers violence, ardour, and zeal.
items.cn: 中古英语时期 vehemence 进入英语，兼指猛烈、激情与狂热。

items.en: Literary and religious senses fade, leaving forceful feeling as the main sense.
items.cn: 现代英语中文学与宗教色彩转淡，主要保留「强烈的感情」这一含义。

note.en: Vehemence is the inward fire made visible; vehement and vehemently carry the same image in adjective and adverb form.
note.cn: vehemence 是让人看得见的内心之火；vehement 与 vehemently 分别以形容词和副词形式承载同一意象。

entries.definition: showing very strong and forceful feeling
entries.definitionCN: 激烈的；强烈的（vehemence 的形容词形式）

entries.definition: in a very forceful and passionate way
entries.definitionCN: 激烈地；强烈地（由形容词加后缀构成）

entries.definition: a rarer variant of vehemence
entries.definitionCN: vehemence 的较少见异形名词

entries.definition: great strength or force of a quality or feeling
entries.definitionCN: 强度；强烈（侧重分量大小，不减情感色彩）

entries.definition: wild, violent anger
entries.definitionCN: 狂怒（情绪更偏向愤怒本身）

entries.definition: a strong feeling or enthusiasm
entries.definitionCN: 激情；热爱（更宽泛，可褒可贬）

normalIntro.en: Vehemence is the noun of vehement, a word for being carried away by fire, so it names the force of feeling that rushes out of a person.
normalIntro.cn: vehemence 是 vehement 的名词，意为被火一样的情感带着走，因此指从人身上冲出来的那股情感力量。

normal.en: The word root vehem- is closely tied to vehement and vehemently.
normal.cn: 词根 vehem- 与 vehement、vehemently 紧密相连。

normal.en: With vehemence is the standard adverb phrase, as in deny something with vehemence.
normal.cn: with vehemence 是常用副词短语，如激烈地否认某事。

normal.en: A speech can be marked by vehemence when the speaker is deeply moved.
normal.cn: 当发言者情绪极深时，一段演说会带上 vehemence。

normal.en: The vehemence of a storm names how hard the wind and rain push.
normal.cn: the vehemence of a storm 指风雨推得多猛。

normal.en: Compare passion: passion is warmer and wider, while vehemence stresses visible force.
normal.cn: 对比 passion：passion 更温暖宽泛，vehemence 强调看得见的猛劲。

abstract.en: Picture a room where every voice suddenly rises and hands strike the table.
abstract.cn: 想象一个屋子，所有声音突然抬高，手掌拍在桌上。

abstract.en: Imagine a speaker leaning forward, words leaving like sparks.
abstract.cn: 想象发言者探身向前，话语像火星一样飞出来。

abstract.en: Think of a gust shoving a window frame until it rattles.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵大风把窗框推得咯咯作响。

examples.en: The chairperson responded with unusual vehemence.
examples.cn: 主席以异乎寻常的激烈态度作出回应。

examples.en: Nobody doubted the vehemence of her opposition to the plan.
examples.cn: 没有人怀疑她对这个计划的反对有多激烈。

examples.en: His vehemence made the quieter members step back.
examples.cn: 他那股激烈的劲头让较沉默的成员纷纷后退。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 vehemence 记成「为河猛伺」：为了过河猛盯着水面；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vehemens（猛烈的、火热的；一说受 vehere「携带、运送」影响）→ 名词 vehementia → 古法语 → 英语 vehemence，核心义「被强烈情感带着走」。

sensesIntro.en: Vehemence begins with visible strength of feeling, then spreads to forceful speech, raging forces of nature, sharp denial, and finally ardent devotion.
sensesIntro.cn: vehemence 从看得见的情感强度出发，再扩展到激烈的话语、狂暴的自然力量、尖锐的否认，最后落到炽热的忠诚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rush of heat that surges out of a person and carries the words along.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股从人身上涌出、把话语一起卷走的热流。

branches.en: Visible strength of feeling is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 看得见的情感强度是日常义项。

branches.en: Forceful speech and fierce denial are aimed versions of the same heat.
branches.cn: 激烈的话语与猛烈的否认是同一股热度对准目标的形态。

branches.en: Raging wind and fire copy the human rush in the physical world.
branches.cn: 狂风烈火把人的奔涌挪到自然界。

branches.en: Lifelong ardour comes from the older sense of fiery zeal.
branches.cn: 一生的炽热源自较早的宗教狂热含义。

branches.en: Both a person and a storm can be said to act with vehemence.
branches.cn: 人和风暴都可以说有 vehemence。

intro.en: Vehemence is a Latin noun ending in -ence, with vehement and vehemently built in the same family.
intro.cn: vehemence 是以 -ence 结尾的拉丁系名词，同一词族还有 vehement 与 vehemently。

latinIntro.en: Latin vehemens means violent or fiery, and its noun vehementia gives the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vehemens 意为猛烈、火热，其名词 vehementia 给了英语这个词。

items.example: Vehemens gives the base meaning.
items.exampleCN: vehemens 提供基础含义。

items.example: Vehementia is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: vehementia 是直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ence marks the quality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ence 标示性质。

items.example: Vehemence names the force of feeling.
items.exampleCN: vehemence 指情感的强度。

items.example: The suffix -ment forms vehement.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ment 构成 vehement。

items.example: Vehement describes forceful feeling.
items.exampleCN: vehement 形容情感猛烈。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms vehemently.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 vehemently。

items.example: Vehemently says how the action is done.
items.exampleCN: vehemently 说明动作方式。

items.example: The suffix -cy gives vehemency.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -cy 构成 vehemency。

items.example: Vehemency is the older variant.
items.exampleCN: vehemency 是较早的异形。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 携带；运送（一般认为与 vehemens 有混淆关系）

definition_zh: 激烈的；强烈的；猛烈的；热烈的
definition_en: showing very strong, forceful feeling, especially in speech or opposition
core_image: 炉膛里的火被一阵风猛地吹起，火舌直抵屋顶
scene: 会场上有人提出一项议案，刚说完便招来反对。The proposal drew a vehement response from the audience.
sceneCN: 这里 vehement 是「激烈的」（第 2 个义项：言辞上的激烈反对或辩护）；句意：这项提案引来听众激烈的回应。

pos.zh: 激烈的；强烈的；猛烈的；热烈的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「激烈；激情」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「激烈地；猛烈地」
较少见的异形名词，义为「激烈；猛烈」

senses.title: Burning with strong feeling
senses.definition: filled with intense, fiery feeling or emotion
senses.definitionCN: 充满炽烈、火热的情感
senses.example: His vehement loyalty to the club never faded.
senses.exampleCN: 他对俱乐部的炽热忠诚从未消退。
senses.why: Latin vehemens meant fiery or violent, and the fire image survives in strong, burning emotion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vehemens 本意是猛烈的、火热的，火这个意象一直保留在「情感炽烈」的含义里。

senses.title: Forceful in opposing or defending
senses.titleCN: 言辞激烈的；激烈反对的
senses.definition: expressing opposition or support in a very forceful and passionate way
senses.definitionCN: 以极有力和热烈的方式表达反对或支持
senses.example: The plan met with vehement opposition from farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划遭到农民的激烈反对。
senses.why: The fire is turned outward against a person or plan, so vehement most often describes forceful speech.
senses.whyCN: 心里的火转向外面的人和计划，于是 vehement 最常形容言辞上的猛烈。

senses.title: Of speech, gesture, or manner
senses.definition: said, shown, or done with great force of voice or movement
senses.definitionCN: 以很大的声音强度或动作幅度说出、表现或做出的
senses.example: He shook his head in vehement refusal.
senses.exampleCN: 他猛烈地摇头表示拒绝。
senses.why: Force that is felt inside also shows in the body, so the word describes how words and gestures are performed.
senses.whyCN: 心里的劲道也会显在身体上，所以这个词也形容话语与手势是「怎么做出的」。

senses.title: Fierce as a physical force
senses.definition: fierce, violent, or powerful, especially of wind, fire, or other natural force
senses.definitionCN: 凶猛的、狂暴有力的，尤指风、火等自然力
senses.example: A vehement wind tore at the thin roof.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵狂风撕扯着薄薄的屋顶。
senses.why: The earliest Latin use was about violent physical force, so the word can still describe nature.
senses.whyCN: 最早期的拉丁语用法本就指物理性的猛烈，因此这个词至今仍能形容自然。

senses.title: Ardent in belief or cause
senses.definition: showing burning zeal or firm commitment to a belief, cause, or person
senses.definitionCN: 对信念、事业或某个人表现出炽热的热忱或坚定投入
senses.example: She was a vehement campaigner for clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一个为清洁水源奔走的热心活动家。
senses.why: In religious and political language the same fire became zeal, so vehement can praise firm, devoted commitment.
senses.whyCN: 在宗教与政治语境里，同一团火化为狂热热忱，所以 vehement 也能称赞坚定的投入。

intro.en: Vehement comes from Latin vehemens, violent or fiery. The form used to be vehemens beside the verb vehere, to carry, and the exact link is generally explained as a scribal confusion, with the deeper details still uncertain.
intro.cn: vehement 来自拉丁语 vehemens（猛烈的、火热的）。早期形式与动词 vehere（携带）并列，一般认为中间发生了书写混淆，更深层的细节仍不确定。

items.en: Vehemens describes violent, fiery, or immoderate things.
items.cn: vehemens 形容猛烈、火热或过度的事物。

items.en: Vehementia is its abstract noun for force of feeling.
items.cn: vehementia 是其表示情感猛烈的抽象名词。

items.en: The adjective takes on intense emotional and religious use.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中该词发展为强烈的情感与宗教用法。

items.en: Vehement appears in English in borrowed French spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，vehement 以借自法语的拼写进入英语。

items.en: The physical sense weakens and forceful speech becomes the dominant use.
items.cn: 现代英语中物理性含义减弱，激烈的言辞成为主流用法。

note.en: Vehement is the adjective of vehemence and pairs with vehemently; its look-alikes include the noun vehemency and unrelated vehicle.
note.cn: vehement 是 vehemence 的形容词，对应副词 vehemently；形近词包括名词 vehemency 与无关的 vehicle。

entries.definition: strong, forceful feeling
entries.definitionCN: 激情；激烈（vehement 的名词形式）

entries.definition: in a forceful, passionate way
entries.definitionCN: 激烈地（由形容词加后缀构成）

entries.definition: a rarer form of vehemence
showing strong romantic or intense feeling
entries.definitionCN: 热情的；充满激情的（更偏个人的热爱）

entries.definition: violent, angry, or aggressive
entries.definitionCN: 凶猛的；激烈的（带攻击色彩）

entries.definition: very enthusiastic and devoted

normalIntro.en: Vehement is the adjective of vehemence; once you see its noun and adverb, the whole family locks together.
normalIntro.cn: vehement 是 vehemence 的形容词；记住它的名词与副词，整个词族就串起来了。

normal.en: The root vehem- echoes Hebrew amen in sound only, with no shared history at all.
normal.cn: 词根 vehem- 在读音上像希伯来语 amen，但两者毫无共同历史。

normal.en: Vehement opposition and vehement denial are the two most common collocations.
normal.cn: vehement opposition 与 vehement denial 是两个最常用的搭配。

normal.en: Adding less makes the antonym less vehement, so compare the two phrases side by side.
normal.cn: 加上 less 就成了「不那么激烈」，把两个说法对照着记。

normal.en: The adverb adds ly, so vehemently keeps the same fire.
normal.cn: 副词加 ly，vehemently 保留同一团火。

normal.en: Compare fierce: fierce stresses attack, while vehement stresses heat of feeling.
normal.cn: 对比 fierce：fierce 强调攻击色彩，vehement 强调情感的热度。

abstract.en: Picture a fire suddenly struck by wind and leaping to the roof.
abstract.cn: 想象一团火突然被风一吹，直蹿到屋顶。

abstract.en: Imagine a speaker whose voice climbs higher with every sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象一位发言者每说一句，嗓门就更高一分。

abstract.en: Think of a window frame shaking hard in a gale.
abstract.cn: 想象窗框在狂风里剧烈晃动。

examples.en: There was vehement applause from the back of the hall.
examples.cn: 大厅后排响起热烈的掌声。

examples.en: She was vehement in her rejection of the offer.
examples.cn: 她强烈地拒绝了这个提议。

examples.en: A vehement protest greeted the new rules.
examples.cn: 新规定一出便引来激烈抗议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 vehement 记成「威核们」：一群核心人物一起发力，威势很猛；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vehemens（猛烈的、火热的；一说与 vehere「携带」混淆有关）→ 古法语 → 英语 vehement，核心义「像火被风带着猛烧」。

sensesIntro.en: Vehement starts from burning emotion, narrows into forceful opposition, spreads to gestures and weather, and ends in devoted zeal.
sensesIntro.cn: vehement 从炽烈的情感出发，收窄到激烈的反对，再扩展到手势与天气，最后落到坚定的热忱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fire in a hearth suddenly driven up by wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：炉膛里的火被风猛地吹得窜高。

branches.en: Burning emotion and devoted zeal are the two sides of the same fire.
branches.cn: 炽烈的情感与执着的热忱是同一团火的两面。

branches.en: Forceful opposition is the most common sense in news and essays.
branches.cn: 激烈的反对是新闻和文章里最常见的义项。

branches.en: Gesture and voice carry the inward force into the open.
branches.cn: 手势与嗓音把内在的劲道带到明处。

branches.en: Wind and fire give the physical sense.
branches.cn: 风与火给出生理层面的猛烈含义。

branches.en: Both sharp words and jerky gestures read as vehement.
branches.cn: 尖锐的话语和急促的手势都算得上激烈。

intro.en: Vehement ends in the Latin adjectival -ent, and the same stem gives vehemence and vehemently.
intro.cn: vehement 以拉丁形容词后缀 -ent 结尾，同一词干还给出 vehemence 与 vehemently。

latinIntro.en: Latin vehemens, violent or fiery, supplies the whole family through its stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vehemens（猛烈、火热）以同一词干供给整个词族。

items.example: Vehemens is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: vehemens 是直接来源。

items.example: Vehementia supplies the noun family.
items.exampleCN: vehementia 供给名词词族。

items.meaningCN: 具有某种性质的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ent marks the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ent 标示形容词。

items.example: Vehement describes forceful feeling.
items.exampleCN: vehement 形容情感猛烈。

items.example: The suffix -ence forms vehemence.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ence 构成 vehemence。

items.example: Vehemence is the matching noun.
items.exampleCN: vehemence 是对应名词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms vehemently.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 vehemently。

items.example: Vehemently modifies verbs of speech.
items.exampleCN: vehemently 修饰说话类动词。

items.example: The phrase less vehement compares two levels of force.
items.exampleCN: 短语 less vehement 用来比较两种猛烈程度。

items.example: The suffix -cy gives vehemency.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -cy 构成 vehemency。

definition_zh: 面纱；遮盖物；隐匿；借口；（修女）头巾
definition_en: a piece of thin cloth worn to cover the face or head, or something that hides or conceals
core_image: 一层半透明的薄纱落下，遮住人的脸，背后的事物变得模糊
scene: 婚礼仪式进行到交换誓言的环节，新娘头部覆着一层薄纱。During the ceremony a fine veil covered the face of the bride.
sceneCN: 这里 veil 是「面纱」（第 1 个义项：遮住脸部的薄织物）；句意：仪式中，一层细薄的面纱罩住了新娘的脸。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 ed 构成，义为「戴面纱的；含蓄的」
由动词加 ing 构成，义为「面纱料；遮掩」
un- 加 veil，义为「揭幕；公布」

senses.title: A cloth covering the face or head
senses.definition: a piece of thin, often light cloth worn to cover the face or the head
senses.definitionCN: 一种薄而轻、遮住脸部或头部的布
senses.example: She lifted her veil as the music stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐停下时，她掀起了面纱。
senses.why: Latin velum is any kind of covering cloth, and the first thing people cover is the face.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 velum 泛指各种遮盖用的布，而人们最先遮住的就是脸。

senses.title: Cloth screening a holy place
senses.definition: a hanging cloth that screens off a sacred or hidden inner room
senses.definitionCN: 隔开神圣或隐蔽内室的悬挂布帘
senses.example: The veil of the temple was torn from top to bottom.
senses.exampleCN: 殿里的帷幕从上到下裂开了。
senses.why: The same cover became a technical term for the curtain hiding the inner sanctuary.
senses.whyCN: 同一种遮盖物在宗教语境里成了专指遮蔽内殿的帷幕。

senses.title: Something that hides or conceals
senses.definition: something that hides a fact, feeling, or situation from view
senses.definitionCN: 把事实、情感或状况遮蔽起来的东西
senses.example: A veil of secrecy hung over the negotiations.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判笼罩着一层隐秘。
senses.why: A cloth that hides a face naturally becomes a metaphor for anything that hides the truth.
senses.whyCN: 遮住脸的布自然而然被用来比喻任何遮盖真相的东西。

senses.title: A covering excuse or pretext
senses.definition: a false outward appearance used to hide a real motive or activity
senses.definitionCN: 用来掩盖真实动机或勾当的虚假外表
senses.example: Extreme measures were taken under the veil of patriotism.
senses.exampleCN: 极端的措施以爱国主义为幌子被推行。
senses.why: When the cover is deliberately kept up, the metaphor turns into an excuse in disguise.
senses.whyCN: 当这层遮盖被人刻意维持，比喻就变成伪装起来的借口。

senses.title: A nun head covering or life
senses.definition: the head covering worn by a nun, or the state of being a nun
senses.definitionCN: 修女佩戴的头巾，或身为修女的状态
senses.example: She took the veil at a small convent in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 她在山间一座小修院披上了修女头巾。
senses.why: Putting on the veil was the public act of entering a convent, so the cloth stands for the whole life.
senses.whyCN: 戴上头巾是进入修院的公开动作，于是这块布就成了整个身份的代称。

senses.title: Membrane on certain organs
senses.definition: one of the membranes found in the mouth or throat of some animals, or attached to an organ
senses.definitionCN: 某些动物口腔或喉部的膜，或附着在器官上的膜
senses.example: The frog closes its eyes behind a translucent veil.
senses.exampleCN: 青蛙在透明的膜后闭上眼睛。
senses.why: Any thin sheet that covers an organ keeps the old meaning of a covering cloth.
senses.whyCN: 任何覆盖器官的薄层都延续了「遮盖物」这一古老含义。

intro.en: Veil goes back to Latin velum, a covering cloth, which is also related to English sail and curtain; it reached English through Old Northern French.
intro.cn: veil 可追溯到拉丁语 velum（遮盖用布），它经古北法语进入英语；与之同源的还有 curtain 等词。

items.en: Reconstructed forms suggest a root for covering or winding round.
items.cn: 重构形式显示有表示遮盖、缠绕的词根。

items.en: Velum means a sail, curtain, or any covering cloth.
items.cn: velum 指帆、帘或任何遮盖用布。

items.en: Veil passes to French and is written veil in northern dialects.
items.cn: velum 进入法语，北部方言写作 veil。

items.en: The English noun first names a cloth covering the face.
items.cn: 英语名词最早指遮盖面部的布。

items.en: Metaphorical and religious uses grow, and the verb develops from the noun.
items.cn: 比喻与宗教用法增多，动词也逐渐由名词衍生出来。

note.en: Veil is a word for covering cloth; its look-alikes include the verb and adjective built on it, plus unrelated near neighbours.
note.cn: veil 是表示遮盖布的词；形近词包括在它上面构成的动词和形容词，以及无关的邻近拼写。

entries.definition: covered with a veil or hidden
entries.definitionCN: 戴面纱的；含蓄的（由 veil 加 ed 构成）

entries.definition: to remove a cover or reveal something
entries.definitionCN: 揭幕；公布（un- 加 veil 构成）

entries.definition: light cloth used for veils
entries.definitionCN: 面纱料；遮掩（veil 的动名词形式）

entries.definition: a piece of cloth hanging at a window or across a stage
entries.definitionCN: 窗帘；帷幕（同为布帘，但用途不同）

entries.definition: a loose outer garment, or something that covers and hides
entries.definitionCN: 斗篷；掩护（也用作掩盖的比喻）

entries.definition: a covering worn over the face, or something that disguises
entries.definitionCN: 面具；伪装（强调遮住身份或真实表情）

normalIntro.en: Veil is a thin cloth; once the cloth is remembered, hidden, holy, and metaphorical senses follow from it.
normalIntro.cn: veil 就是一层薄布；记住这块布，隐藏、神圣与比喻的义项就顺着来了。

normal.en: Veil sits in a family with veiled, unveil, and veiling.
normal.cn: veil 与 veiled、unveil、veiling 属于同一词族。

normal.en: Draw a veil over something means to stop talking about it.
normal.cn: draw a veil over 某事，意思是别再谈它了。

normal.en: Under the veil of is a common phrase for pretending reasons.
normal.cn: under the veil of 是表达虚假借口的常见说法。

normal.en: To take the veil is the old phrase for becoming a nun.
normal.cn: take the veil 是「当修女」的老说法。

normal.en: Compare mask: a mask hides the face, while a veil softens it.
normal.cn: 对比 mask：面具把脸遮住，面纱只是把脸柔化。

abstract.en: Picture a bride lifting a thin white cloth from her face.
abstract.cn: 想象新娘从脸上撩起一层薄薄的白布。

abstract.en: Imagine a stage rising with a heavy cloth that hides the inner room.
abstract.cn: 想象一块厚重的布垂下来，遮住里侧的房间。

abstract.en: Think of fog softening a row of houses into shapes.
abstract.cn: 想象雾气把一排房子化成模糊的轮廓。

examples.en: A thin veil covered her face during the ceremony.
examples.cn: 仪式中一层薄纱罩住了她的脸。

examples.en: He drew a veil over his past mistakes.
examples.cn: 他对过去的错误避而不谈。

examples.en: The government unveiled a new policy last week.
examples.cn: 政府上周公布了一项新政策。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 veil 记成「围了」：四周围了一层薄布，脸就看不见了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 velum（遮盖用布、帆、帘）→ 古北法语 veil → 英语 veil，核心义「一层罩住东西的薄布」。

sensesIntro.en: Veil starts as a face cloth, gains holy and metaphorical covering senses, then extends to a pretext, to a nun life, and to membranes.
sensesIntro.cn: veil 从遮脸的布出发，长出神圣与比喻性的遮盖义，再扩展到借口、修女身份与膜状结构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin cloth dropped over the face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层薄布垂落在脸的上面。

branches.en: Face cloth and temple curtain are the two concrete cloth senses.
branches.cn: 面纱与殿内帷幕是两种具体的布义项。

branches.en: Secrecy and mystery come from the metaphor of the cloth.
branches.cn: 隐秘与神秘由这层布的比喻而来。

branches.en: A kept-up cover becomes an excuse.
branches.cn: 刻意维持的遮盖就成了借口。

branches.en: The nun head covering stands for the whole vocation.
branches.cn: 修女头巾代指整个身份。

branches.en: Both a bridal veil and an organ membrane are thin covering sheets.
branches.cn: 新娘面纱与器官薄膜都是薄薄的覆盖层。

intro.en: Veil is built on Latin velum, with un- forming unveil and the -ed and -ing forms giving veiled and veiling.
intro.cn: veil 建立在拉丁语 velum 之上，un- 构成 unveil，-ed 与 -ing 给出 veiled 与 veiling。

latinIntro.en: Latin velum means a cloth for covering and is related to words for sail and curtain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 velum 意为遮盖用的布，与表示帆、帘的词语相关。

items.example: Velum is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: velum 是直接来源。

items.example: French veil reaches English early.
items.exampleCN: 法语 veil 早期进入英语。

items.example: Veil keeps the noun sense.
items.exampleCN: veil 保留名词含义。

items.example: Veil works as verb from the noun.
items.exampleCN: veil 由名词转为动词。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms veiled.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 veiled。

items.example: Veiled describes hidden meanings.
items.exampleCN: veiled 描述隐藏的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms veiling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 veiling。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unveil.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unveil。

items.example: Unveil means taking the cover off.
items.exampleCN: unveil 表示把掩盖拿掉。

definition_zh: 毒液；毒；怨恨；恶意；恶毒的言辞
definition_en: the poison produced by snakes, spiders and some other animals, and by extension intense hatred or spiteful feeling
core_image: 毒蛇抬起颈子，尖牙上挂着一滴透明毒液，正要滴下
scene: 灌木丛里一条蛇竖起前半身，发出嘶嘶声，行人立刻退到小路另一边。The ranger warned us that one bite from this snake could deliver enough venom to kill an adult.

collocations.zh: 满怀怨恨地；恶狠狠地说

senses.title: The poison of a snake or spider
senses.definition: the poisonous liquid that snakes, spiders, scorpions and some other animals produce and inject by biting or stinging
senses.definitionCN: 蛇、蜘蛛、蝎子等动物分泌并通过咬或蜇注入的有毒液体
senses.example: Antivenom is made by slowly exposing horses to small doses of snake venom.
senses.exampleCN: 抗蛇毒血清是通过让马逐渐接触少量蛇毒制成的。
senses.why: Latin venenum meant a drug or potion, and in use it narrowed to a deadly drink, so the animal poison keeps the image of a dangerous liquid.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 venenum 原指药水、药剂，后来窄化为能致命的饮剂，所以动物的毒也保留「危险液体」的意象。

senses.title: Poison used to wound a person
senses.definition: a poison used to hurt or kill, especially when carried in a weapon, arrow or drink
senses.definitionCN: 用来伤害或杀死人的毒物，尤指藏在武器、箭头或饮品中的毒
senses.example: In old stories the king is killed by venom poured into his cup.
senses.exampleCN: 在古代故事里，国王被倒进杯中的毒药害死。
senses.why: Once the word names any deadly potion, it can label poison placed in a drink or on a blade, not only what an animal makes.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指任何致命的药液，它就能指放进酒里或涂在刀刃上的毒，而不只限于动物分泌的东西。

senses.title: Intense hatred or spite
senses.definition: a feeling of great spite or bitterness that someone shows in words or looks
senses.definitionCN: 某人用言语或神情表现出的强烈怨恨与狠毒
senses.example: Her voice was full of venom when she described the betrayal.
senses.exampleCN: 她描述那次背叛时，声音里满是怨恨。
senses.why: A poison that burns inside is a natural picture for bitter speech, so the physical liquid became a metaphor for hatred.
senses.whyCN: 在体内灼烧的毒，正好可以用来比喻刻薄的话语，于是有形的液体成了怨恨的隐喻。

senses.title: Spiteful or malicious words
senses.definition: harsh and malicious words aimed at someone
senses.definitionCN: 针对某人的尖刻而恶毒的话
senses.example: He spat venom at his opponents in the final debate.
senses.exampleCN: 在最后一场辩论中他朝对手喷出恶毒的话。
senses.why: The metaphor moves from the feeling to its outlet, so venom also names the words that carry hatred.
senses.whyCN: 隐喻从情绪迁移到出口，因此 venom 也指承载怨恨的话语本身。

senses.title: A powerful harmful force
senses.definition: a source of harm that spreads quickly like poison, used of gossip, influence or ideology
senses.definitionCN: 像毒一样迅速扩散的伤害来源，用于流言、影响力或意识形态
senses.example: Social media spread the rumour like venom through the small town.
senses.exampleCN: 社交媒体让这则谣言像毒一样在小镇里蔓延。
senses.why: Anything that corrupts quietly while looking harmless can borrow the poison image and become venom in a looser sense.
senses.whyCN: 任何看似无害却悄悄腐蚀的事物都能借用「毒」的意象，在更宽泛的意义上成为 venom。

intro.en: Venom comes through Old French from Latin venenum, a drug, potion or poison, and is akin to Venus, so a love charm and a deadly potion once shared one word.
intro.cn: venom 经古法语来自拉丁语 venenum（药剂、药水、毒药）。它与 Venus 同族：最初表示药剂（包括春药），后来多指有毒的药水。

items.en: Venenum means a drug, a potion, a love charm or a poison.
items.cn: venenum 指药剂、药水、春药或毒药。

items.en: Pliny and other writers use venenum mainly for deadly poison.
items.cn: 普林尼等作家主要用 venenum 表示致命毒药。

items.en: Venim, later venin, carries both drug and poison meanings.
items.cn: 古法语 venim（后作 venin）兼有药剂与毒药两义。

items.en: Venim and venym are recorded for poison around 1300.
items.cn: 约十三世纪末，venim 与 venym 已用来表示毒药。

items.en: Poison narrows to animals, while a figurative use for hatred grows.
items.cn: 毒义逐渐专指动物的毒，同时衍生出「怨恨」的比喻用法。

note.en: Venom looks like venial and venomous and is akin to Venus, while its near meanings sit beside poison, toxin and malice.
note.cn: venom 与 venomous 同族，与 venial 只是拼写相近；它的近义邻居则是 poison、toxin 与 malice。

normalIntro.en: Venom is a deadly liquid: it comes from Latin venenum, once just a drug, and it can also stand for a hatred that burns inside.

normal.en: Snake venom is injected through fangs.

normal.en: Poison comes from the Greek for drink; venom is what an animal injects.

normal.en: With venom means in a bitterly angry way.
normal.cn: with venom 表示充满怨恨地。

normal.en: The adjective venomous keeps the whole word and adds the suffix -ous.

normal.cn: 对比 toxin：toxin 是实验室用语，泛指生物制造的毒物。

abstract.en: Picture a clear drop hanging on a fang, ready to fall.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴透明的毒液挂在尖牙上，正要落下。

abstract.en: See a king drinking from a cup with a bitter aftertaste.
abstract.cn: 想象一位国王饮下一杯留有苦味的酒。

abstract.en: Hear a voice that spits every word like droplets of poison.
abstract.cn: 听见一个声音，每个字都像毒液一样喷出来。

examples.en: Scientists study how snake venom affects the nervous system.
examples.cn: 科学家研究蛇毒如何影响神经系统。

examples.en: The venom left the victim paralysed within minutes.
examples.cn: 毒液让受害者在几分钟内就瘫痪了。

examples.en: He spoke with such venom that the whole room fell silent.
examples.cn: 他说得如此恶毒，整个房间顿时安静下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「venom」近似「喂脓」——把毒喂进伤口，必然化脓；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

sensesIntro.en: Venom starts as the poison an animal injects, then becomes any deadly potion, and finally the hatred that burns inside people and the words that carry it.
sensesIntro.cn: venom 先是动物注入的毒液，再泛指致命的毒物，最后转为人心里的怨恨以及承载怨恨的话语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of poison hanging from a fang.
core.cn: 核心意象：尖牙上挂着的一滴毒液。

branches.en: The deadly liquid itself: fangs, blades and cups all carry it.
branches.cn: 致命液体本身：尖牙、刀刃与酒杯都能承载它。

branches.en: The feeling line: hatred borrowed the picture of a poison inside.
branches.cn: 情绪线：怨恨借用了「体内有毒」的意象。

branches.en: The speech line: words become the visible output of that poison.
branches.cn: 言语线：话语成为这种毒看得见的出口。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of a hidden, slow-acting harm.
branches.cn: 两个义项共有「隐秘、缓慢发作的伤害」这一观念。

branches.en: Anything spreading unnoticed behaves like venom in the looser sense.
branches.cn: 任何悄悄扩散的事物，在宽泛意义上都像 venom。

intro.cn: venom 是拉丁语借词，其词族由形容词 venomous 与副词 venomously 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin venenum meant a drug or poison and is related to Venus; the suffix -ous turns it into an adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 venenum 意为药剂或毒药，与 Venus 同源；英语后缀 -ous 把它变成形容词。

items.example: Venom narrows towards animal poison.

items.example: Venomed often describes an arrow.
items.exampleCN: venomed 常形容箭。

senses.title: Able to inject poison
senses.definition: producing venom and able to poison a person or animal by biting or stinging
senses.definitionCN: 能分泌毒液，并通过咬或蜇使人或动物中毒的
senses.example: Only a few of the snakes in this region are venomous.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区只有少数几种蛇是有毒的。
senses.why: The noun venom plus the adjective suffix -ous gives the plain meaning of possessing venom.
senses.whyCN: 名词 venom 加形容词后缀 -ous，直接表示「具有毒液」。

senses.title: Poisonous in a scientific sense
senses.definition: of a bite, sting or substance: charged with venom and able to cause harm when it enters the body
senses.definitionCN: 指咬伤、蜇刺或物质含有毒液，进入身体后会造成伤害
senses.example: Biologists measured how far a venomous bite could reach through the boot.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家测量了带毒的咬伤能穿透靴子多远。
senses.why: Field use moves from the animal to what it delivers, so the adjective also describes the poisoned result.
senses.whyCN: 野外用法从动物本身转向它释放的东西，所以这个形容词也描述中毒的后果。

senses.title: Full of bitter hatred
senses.definition: showing strong anger and the wish to hurt someone with words or looks
senses.definitionCN: 用言语或神情表现出强烈愤怒和伤害他人意愿的
senses.example: She gave him a venomous look before leaving the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她恶狠狠地看了他一眼，然后离开了房间。
senses.why: The poison metaphor makes hatred feel like a liquid burning inside, so the adjective also paints the look that carries it.
senses.whyCN: 毒液的隐喻让怨恨像体内燃烧的液体，因此这个形容词也能形容承载怨恨的眼神。

senses.title: Marked by malicious words
senses.definition: using words meant to wound, as in a cruel review, letter or remark
senses.definitionCN: 用意在伤人的话语，如刻薄的评论、信件或言论
senses.example: The newspaper printed a venomous review of the new play.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸登了一篇对新剧刻薄的评论。
senses.why: Because the adjective can modify speech, it works for essays, reviews and letters as well as for animals.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个形容词能修饰言语，它既可用于动物，也可用于文章、评论与信件。

senses.title: Spreading harm like poison
senses.definition: spreading harmful influence quietly, used of rumours, ideas or campaigns
senses.definitionCN: 悄然散布有害影响的，用于流言、观念或运动
senses.example: Rumours proved more venomous than the disease itself in the crowded camp.
senses.exampleCN: 在拥挤的营地里，流言比疾病本身更有害。
senses.why: A loose extension treats anything that corrupts quietly as a poison, hence a more general sense of harmful.
senses.whyCN: 宽泛的引申把任何悄然腐败的事物都视为毒，于是产生了更一般的「有害」义。

intro.en: Venomous joins the noun venom, from Latin venenum, with the English suffix -ous, so it means simply full of venom.
intro.cn: venomous 由名词 venom（源自拉丁语 venenum）加英语后缀 -ous 构成，字面意思就是「充满毒液的」。

items.en: Venenum, a drug or poison, stands behind the noun.
items.cn: 拉丁语 venenum（药剂、毒药）是名词的来源。

items.en: Venim, later venin, reaches English as a poison word.
items.cn: 古法语 venim（后作 venin）以「毒」义进入英语。

items.en: Venom names poison in English from around 1300.
items.cn: 约十三世纪末，venom 在英语中表示毒。

items.en: The suffix -ous builds venomous as an adjective of full of.
items.cn: 后缀 -ous 把 venomous 构成「充满……的」形容词。

items.en: The figurative sense for spiteful speech is well established.
items.cn: 比喻义「恶毒的言语」已经完全确立。

note.en: Venomous is the adjective of venom and looks like venial; its near meanings are poisonous, toxic and spiteful.
note.cn: venomous 是 venom 的形容词形式，与 venial 只是拼写相近；它的近义邻居是 poisonous、toxic 与 spiteful。

normal.en: Venom plus -ous gives venomous, as danger gives dangerous.

normal.en: A venomous snake injects venom; a poisonous frog only harms when eaten.

abstract.en: See a drop of poison on a glove after a sting.

abstract.en: Hear a whispered remark that leaves the room cold.
abstract.cn: 听见一句低语，让整个房间冷下来。

examples.en: The zoo keeps several venomous species behind thick glass.
examples.cn: 动物园在厚玻璃后养着几种有毒的物种。

examples.en: He answered the question with a venomous smile.
examples.cn: 他用一个恶毒的微笑回答了这个问题。

examples.en: Not every brightly coloured frog is venomous.

sensesIntro.en: From an animal that carries venom, the adjective borrows the poison for its bite, for bitter hatred in the face, for wounding words, and for any quietly harmful force.

branches.en: The wound line: the bite or sting itself borrows the word.

branches.en: The feeling and speech lines: hatred in the eyes and in the words.

branches.en: The idea line: harmful influence spreads like poison.

branches.en: Both senses keep the same inside picture of poison that burns.

senses.title: Supplying fresh air to a room
senses.definition: the process of letting fresh air into a room or building and stale air out
senses.definitionCN: 让新鲜空气进入房间或建筑、把污浊空气排出去的过程
senses.example: Good ventilation is the simplest way to keep a crowded classroom healthy.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的通风是让拥挤教室保持健康的最简单办法。
senses.why: Latin ventulus means a light breeze and ventilare means to fan, so ventilation is originally the act of fanning air through a space.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ventulus 意为微风，ventilare 意为扇风，所以 ventilation 最初就是把空气扇动、穿过某个空间的动作。

senses.title: Equipment that moves air
senses.definition: the equipment, shafts and fans installed to move air through a building
senses.definitionCN: 为让空气在建筑内流动而安装的设备、风道与风扇
senses.example: The hotel was renovated and a new ventilation system was fitted on every floor.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店翻修后，每一层都装了新的通风系统。
senses.why: When the action becomes a fixed installation, the same noun names the machinery that does the job.
senses.whyCN: 当动作固定为长期设施时，同一个名词也就指承担这项工作的一整套设备。

senses.title: Open public discussion
senses.definition: the act of making an issue known and discussed openly
senses.definitionCN: 把某个问题公开出来并加以讨论的行为
senses.example: The report called for more ventilation of concerns about data privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 报告呼吁更公开地讨论数据隐私方面的担忧。
senses.why: Air that is let out is a natural picture of thoughts let out, so ventilation inherits the Latin legal sense of bringing a matter into the open.
senses.whyCN: 让空气出去，是让思绪出去的自然图景，因此 ventilation 继承了拉丁语法律用语「把问题摊到明处」的含义。

senses.title: Mechanical help with breathing
senses.definition: in medicine, the use of a machine to move air in and out of the lungs
senses.definitionCN: 医学上用机器帮助空气进出肺部
senses.example: The patient was kept alive on ventilation for several days.
senses.exampleCN: 这位病人靠人工通气维持了几天生命。
senses.why: Because the word describes moving air through a space, it is applied to the lungs as a space that needs air moved through it.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词描述的是让空气通过某个空间，它自然可以用于肺：肺也是需要空气穿过的空间。

senses.title: The natural flow of air
senses.definition: the way air actually flows through a space, as in the phrase ventilation rate
senses.definitionCN: 空气在空间中实际流动的状况，如通风量这一说法
senses.example: The engineers measured the ventilation rate of every room in the lab.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师测量了实验室每个房间的通风量。
senses.why: Scientists turned the general noun into a measurable quantity, so ventilation also labels the flow itself.
senses.whyCN: 科学家把一般名词变成可测量的量，因此 ventilation 也指空气流动本身。

intro.en: Ventilation comes from Latin ventilare, to fan or winnow, built on ventulus, a light breeze, and in Roman law it already meant bringing a matter into the open.
intro.cn: ventilation 来自拉丁语 ventilare（扇风、扬谷），源于 ventulus（微风）；在罗马法律用语中它还表示「把案子摊到明处」。

items.en: Ventulus, a light breeze, comes from ventus, wind.
items.cn: ventulus 意为微风，来自 ventus（风）。

items.en: Ventilare means to fan, to winnow grain, and to bring a matter into the open.
items.cn: ventilare 意为扇风、扬谷，也指把问题公开。

items.en: Ventilatio covers both fanning air and legal ventilation of a case.
items.cn: ventilatio 兼指扇动空气与案件的法律澄清。

items.en: Ventilation enters English as a medical and building term.
items.cn: ventilation 以医学与建筑术语的身份进入英语。

items.en: Mechanical and industrial ventilation creates the equipment sense.
items.cn: 机械与工业通风带来了「设备」这一义项。

note.en: Ventilation is the English noun from Latin ventilare, and it looks like vent, ventilate and ventilator; its neighbours are airflow, aeration and circulation.
note.cn: ventilation 是 ventilate 的名词形式，与 vent、ventilation 形状相关；语义邻居则是 airflow、aeration 与 circulation。

entries.definition: an opening that lets air in or out
to move fresh air into a space
a device or a machine that moves air
the movement of air through a space
the process of putting air into soil or water
the movement of air or liquid in a closed space

normalIntro.en: Ventilation is the English noun from Latin ventilare, to fan, built on ventus, wind.
normalIntro.cn: ventilation 是来自拉丁语 ventilare（扇风）的名词，源于 ventus（风）。

normal.en: Ventus means wind, so every form of this family keeps the air picture.
normal.cn: ventus 意为风，因此这一词族的每个形式都保留「空气」的意象。

normal.en: Natural ventilation uses windows; mechanical ventilation uses fans.
normal.cn: natural ventilation 靠窗户；mechanical ventilation 靠风机。

normal.en: A ventilation shaft is a vertical passage for air.
normal.cn: ventilation shaft 是让空气通行的竖井。

normal.en: Ventilation of a question means bringing it out for open talk.
normal.cn: ventilation of a question 指把问题拿出来公开讨论。

normal.en: Compare vent: vent is the hole, ventilation is the whole process.
normal.cn: 对比 vent：vent 是那个孔，ventilation 是整个过程。

abstract.en: Picture a window pushed open and stale air curling out.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇窗被推开，浊气卷着往外散。

abstract.en: See a row of vents along a factory wall, each pulling air.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂墙上一排排气口，各自抽着风。

abstract.en: Hear a closed meeting finally throw its windows open to public talk.
abstract.cn: 想象一场闭门会议终于向公众敞开门窗。

examples.en: Poor ventilation helps infections spread quickly through a school.
examples.cn: 通风不良会让感染在学校里迅速传播。

examples.en: The builders installed a new ventilation system in the basement.
examples.cn: 建筑工人在地下室安装了新的通风系统。

examples.en: The committee asked for full ventilation of the safety report.
examples.cn: 委员会要求充分公开讨论这份安全报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ventilation」前半截像「文提」——把文气（空气）提进屋里，就是通风；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ventus（风）+ 指小后缀 -ulus → ventulus（微风）→ ventilare（扇风；扬谷；公开）→ 晚期拉丁 ventilatio → 英语 ventilation。同族有 vent、ventilate、ventilator，核心义是「让空气穿过一个空间」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun starts as an act of moving air, becomes the machinery that does it, then opens into public discussion, mechanical breathing and measurable airflow.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词先是让空气流动的动作，再指承担这项工作的设备，随后延伸到公开讨论、机械呼吸以及可测量的空气流量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a window pushed wide open to let the stale air out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇被推开的窗，把浊气放出去。

branches.en: The act line: fresh air in, stale air out.
branches.cn: 动作线：放进新鲜空气，排出浊气。

branches.en: The machinery line: fans, shafts and systems that keep the air moving.
branches.cn: 设备线：风机、风道与系统让空气持续流动。

branches.en: The public line: issues carried into the open like air.
branches.cn: 公开线：问题像空气一样被带到明处。

branches.en: The body line: the lungs are a space that needs air moved.
branches.cn: 身体线：肺也是需要空气穿过的空间。

branches.en: The natural flow and its measurement describe one and the same air.
branches.cn: 自然流动与它的测量描述的是同一股空气。

intro.en: Ventilation sits at the end of a family from Latin ventus, with vent, ventilate, ventilator and ventilated around it.
intro.cn: ventilation 位于源自拉丁语 ventus 的词族末端，周围有 vent、ventilate、ventilator 与 ventilated。

latinIntro.en: Latin ventus means wind, the suffix -ulus gives ventulus, a light breeze, and ventilare turns it into the verb to fan.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ventus 意为风，后缀 -ulus 构成 ventulus（微风），ventilare 则把它变成动词「扇风」。

items.example: Ventus is the root of the family.
items.exampleCN: ventus 是这一词族的词根。

items.example: Ventulus is built with the dimutive suffix.
items.exampleCN: ventulus 由指小后缀构成。

items.meaning: to fan, winnow, bring into the open
items.example: Ventilare gives the English verb.
items.exampleCN: ventilare 提供英语动词。

items.example: Late Latin ventilationem is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 晚期拉丁语 ventilationem 是直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms a noun of process.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成表过程的名词。

items.meaning: the process or system of moving air
items.example: Ventilation keeps the process sense.
items.exampleCN: ventilation 保留过程含义。

items.example: Ventilate is the shorter verb.
items.exampleCN: ventilate 是较短的动词。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -or forms ventilator.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 构成 ventilator。

items.example: Ventilator names the machine.
items.exampleCN: ventilator 指机器。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms ventilated.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 ventilated。

definition_zh: 会场；举办地；比赛场地；举办场所；地点
definition_en: the place where an event, meeting, or performance takes place
core_image: 一群人从各处赶来，汇聚到同一扇门口
scene: 考试前，学生和监考老师陆续走进同一栋大楼登记入场。Before the exam, students and invigilators streamed into the same venue to register at the door.
sceneCN: 这里 venue 是「场地、会场」（第 1 个义项：活动或聚会的举办地点）；句意：考试前，学生和监考老师陆续走进同一栋大楼登记入场。

pos.zh: 会场；举办地；地点；比赛场地

collocations.phrase: the venue for the Olympic Games

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁动词 venia（宽恕）派生，义为「可宽恕的、轻微的」
由前缀 con-（一起）+ venire（来）构成，义为「召集；集会」
由法语的「前来」义演变，义为「大街；通道」

senses.title: The place where an event is held
senses.definition: the place where a concert, meeting, or other organised event takes place
senses.definitionCN: 音乐会、会议或其他组织性活动举行的地点
senses.example: The hotel is a popular venue for business conferences.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店是很受欢迎的商业会议场地。
senses.why: Venue descends from Latin venire, to come, because a venue is where people come together for an event.
senses.whyCN: venue 来自拉丁语 venire（来），因为 venue 就是大家「来」到一处参加活动的地方。

senses.title: A location for a sporting match
senses.definition: the stadium or ground where a sports match or competition is played
senses.definitionCN: 举行体育比赛或赛事的体育场或场地
senses.example: The team moved the match to a neutral venue.
senses.exampleCN: 这支球队把比赛转移到中立的场地举行。
senses.why: Sport borrows the same attendance sense: a stadium is a place teams and crowds come to.
senses.whyCN: 体育沿用「人群聚集处」这一层含义：体育场就是球队和观众汇聚而来的地方。

senses.title: The location of a court trial
senses.definition: the court or district where a legal case is officially heard
senses.definitionCN: 正式受理法律案件的法院或司法管辖区
senses.example: The judge agreed to a change of venue for the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 法官同意为这次审判更换审理地点。
senses.why: Law asks where the parties should come, so venue became a formal term for the proper place of a case.
senses.whyCN: 法律先问当事人该到哪里去，于是 venue 成为案件法定审理地的正式说法。

senses.title: The literal act of coming
senses.definition: the old sense of a coming or an arrival, a person or thing that comes
senses.definitionCN: 旧义：前来、到达，以及到来的人或事物
senses.example: In early records the word named a coming rather than a place.
senses.exampleCN: 在早期文献里，这个词指「到来」而非「地点」。
senses.why: The oldest layer is simply the act of coming; the place sense grew out of it later.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的一层含义就是「来」这个动作，「地点」义是后来从它长出来的。

intro.en: Venue comes from Old French venue, a coming, from the feminine past participle of venir, to come, which goes back to Latin venire.
intro.cn: venue 来自古法语 venue（到来），是动词 venir（来）的阴性过去分词，其源头是拉丁语 venire。

items.en: Venire means to come, and its past participle is ventum.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，其过去分词是 ventum。

items.en: Venir means to come, and venue is its feminine past participle.
items.cn: 古法语 venir 意为「来」，venue 是其阴性过去分词。

items.en: Venue enters English with the sense of a coming or arrival.
items.cn: venue 以「到来、到达」之义进入英语。

items.en: Law adopts venue for the place where a case is heard.
items.cn: 法律领域采用 venue，指案件的审理地点。

items.en: The word widens to any place where an event or show takes place.
items.cn: 词义扩大到任何活动或演出的举办地点。

items.en: Venue now names stadiums, halls, and online meeting spaces.
items.cn: 如今 venue 可指体育场、大厅，甚至线上会议空间。

note.en: Venue shares the Latin root venire with convene, avenue, intervene, and is close to place words such as site, location, and setting.
note.cn: venue 与 convene、avenue、intervene 共享拉丁语词根 venire，并且与 site、location、setting 这类「地点」词相邻。

entries.definition: to bring people together for a meeting
to become involved in a situation in order to change it
a broad road, or a way of reaching something
a place where something is built or happens
a particular position or place
the place and surroundings in which something happens

normalIntro.en: Venue is the place people come to: the same root as convene, to come together.
normalIntro.cn: venue 是「大家来的地方」：它与 convene（聚集）同根。

normal.en: A venue is where an event happens, so book the venue early.
normal.cn: venue 是活动举行处，所以要早点预订场地。

normal.en: The conference venue was a hotel near the station.
normal.cn: 会议场地是车站附近的一家酒店。

normal.en: The Olympic venue was rebuilt for the new games.
normal.cn: 奥运场馆为新一届赛事做了重建。

normal.en: In law, a change of venue means moving where a case is heard.
normal.cn: 在法律里，change of venue 指变更审理地点。

normal.en: Sports journalists often call a stadium the venue.
normal.cn: 体育记者常把体育场称为 venue。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd of people all walking toward one lit gateway.
abstract.cn: 想象一大群人一起走向一扇亮着灯的大门。

abstract.en: Imagine players running onto the same pitch on match day.
abstract.cn: 想象比赛日球员们跑上同一片草场。

abstract.en: Think of a courtroom where the parties must officially appear.
abstract.cn: 想象一间法庭，双方当事人都必须正式到场。

examples.en: The conference venue has space for more than a thousand guests.
examples.cn: 会议场地可容纳一千多位客人。

examples.en: Organisers chose a smaller venue to keep the concert intimate.
examples.cn: 组织者选了更小的场地，让音乐会保持亲切氛围。

examples.en: The court moved the hearing to another venue.
examples.cn: 法院把听证会移到另一个地点举行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「温床」——venue 读起来像「温床」，人们都来「温床」聚集，于是指场地；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 venire（来）→ 古法语 venir 的过去分词 venue（到来）→ 中古英语 venue（到来）→ 现代英语 venue（场所、场地），核心义由「来」转为「人们来到之处」。

sensesIntro.en: Venue begins with the act of coming, moves into the law for the place of a case, and settles on any place where events or sports take place.
sensesIntro.cn: venue 从「到来」这一动作出发，经法律领域指案件审理地，最后固定为活动或比赛的举办场所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: people converging on one doorway.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群汇聚到同一扇门口。

branches.en: A concert hall or hotel is where an event takes place.
branches.cn: 音乐厅或酒店是活动举行的场所。

branches.en: A stadium is the same idea applied to sport.
branches.cn: 体育场是把同一概念用于体育赛事。

branches.en: A court venue is the formal place a case must come to.
branches.cn: court venue 是案件必须到达的法定地点。

branches.en: The original act of coming is the seed of all the place senses.
branches.cn: 「到来」这一原始动作是所有地点义项的种子。

branches.en: Both event spaces and sports grounds are places crowds come to watch.
branches.cn: 活动场地与运动场都是人群前来观看的地方。

intro.en: Venue is built on the Latin verb venire, and English words such as convene, intervene, and avenue share that family.
intro.cn: venue 建立在拉丁语动词 venire 之上，convene、intervene、avenue 等英语词都属于这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire means to come, and its participle ventum feeds venue, convene, and prevent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 venire 意为「来」，其分词形式 ventum 滋养了 venue、convene 与 prevent。

items.example: Venire gives the idea of people coming together.
items.exampleCN: venire 提供「人们前来」的意思。

items.example: Ventum is the past participle of venire.
items.exampleCN: ventum 是 venire 的过去分词。

items.example: Old French venir carries the Latin verb into French.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 venir 把拉丁语动词带进法语。

items.example: Venue is the source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: venue 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: Con- plus venire forms convene.
items.exampleCN: con- 加 venire 构成 convene。

items.example: To convene is to make people come together.
items.exampleCN: convene 就是让人们聚在一起。

items.example: Inter- plus venire forms intervene.
items.exampleCN: inter- 加 venire 构成 intervene。

items.example: An avenue is a way that leads to a place.
items.exampleCN: avenue 是通往某处的路。

items.example: Prevent comes from pre- plus venire, to come before.
items.exampleCN: prevent 由 pre- 与 venire 构成，即「先来一步」。

items.example: Venial comes from Latin venia, pardon.
items.exampleCN: venial 来自拉丁语 venia（宽恕）。

definition_zh: 翠绿的；青葱的；年轻不谙世事的
definition_en: covered with green grass or plants, and therefore fresh and full of life
core_image: 雨后的山坡，草叶被雨水洗得发亮
scene: 雨停后，旅人站在窗前，看见山坡上青草正冒出新芽。After the rain, the traveller stood by the window and saw verdant slopes fresh with new grass.
sceneCN: 这里 verdant 是「青葱翠绿的」（第 1 个义项：长满绿草和植物的）；句意：雨停后，旅人站在窗前，看见山坡上青草正冒出新芽。

pos.zh: 翠绿的；青葱的；年轻不谙世事的

derivatives.zh: 由 Latin viridis 经古法语 verdor 而来的名词，义为「青翠、草木葱茏」
由古法语 vert de Grèce（希腊之绿）演变，义为「铜绿」
由 verdant 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「葱翠地」

senses.title: Green with growing plants
senses.titleCN: 绿意盎然的；长满草木的
senses.definition: covered with lush green grass, trees, or plants
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖着茂密的绿草、树木或植物
senses.example: The valley was verdant after the spring rains.
senses.exampleCN: 春雨过后，山谷一片葱绿。
senses.why: The Latin spelling was virid-, with an i, so a northern French form virdant kept the i and produced our verdant.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词干写作 virid-（带 i），北部法语形式 virdant 保留了这个 i，于是产生英语 verdant。

senses.title: Fresh and full of life
senses.definition: fresh, lively, and flourishing, as if newly grown
senses.definitionCN: 清新、有活力、蓬勃发展的，仿佛刚刚长出
senses.example: A verdant imagination kept the young writer productive.
senses.exampleCN: 丰富的想象让这位年轻作家一直笔耕不辍。
senses.why: Green foliage stands for new growth, so the green colour easily shifts into freshness and vitality.
senses.whyCN: 绿色枝叶是新生长的象征，于是「绿」很自然地引申为「清新、有活力」。

senses.title: Young and inexperienced
senses.definition: used of a person, young and inexperienced, literally green
senses.definitionCN: 用于人，指年轻幼稚、缺乏经验，字面就是「青」
senses.example: The old soldiers smiled at the verdant recruits.
senses.exampleCN: 老兵们看着这些青涩的新兵笑了笑。
senses.why: English calls an inexperienced person green, and this literary adjective carries the same young and green idea.
senses.whyCN: 英语里本就用 green 形容缺乏经验的人，这个文学化形容词沿用同一层「青涩」的联想。

intro.en: Verdant goes back to Latin viridis, green, through northern Old French virdant, and it is related to vert, verdure, and verde.
intro.cn: verdant 追溯到拉丁语 viridis（绿色的），经北部古法语 virdant 而来，与 vert、verdure、verde 同源。

items.en: Viridis means green, and virere means to be green or vigorous.
items.cn: viridis 意为「绿色的」，virere 意为「发绿、茂盛」。

items.en: The northern form virdant keeps the i of the Latin stem; the standard form verdant drops it.
items.cn: 北部法语形式 virdant 保留了拉丁语词干的 i，标准形式 verdant 则脱落了它。

items.en: Verdant is recorded in the sixteenth century as a poetic word for green.
items.cn: verdant 在十六世纪被记录为表示「绿色」的诗歌用词。

items.en: The word covers green land, fresh growth, and figurative youth.
items.cn: 该词涵盖绿地、新生的草木以及比喻意义上的年轻。

items.en: Verdant appears in travel writing, gardening, and sustainability slogans.
items.cn: verdant 常见于旅行写作、园艺以及环保口号中。

note.en: Verdant belongs to the Latin green family with virid, verdure, and vert, and it sits near green, lush, and leafy.
note.cn: verdant 属于以拉丁语 virid 为核心的「绿色」词族，身边有 verdure、vert，以及 green、lush、leafy 这些近义词。

entries.definition: greenness and fresh plant growth
a green coating on copper
literary and technical term for green
entries.definitionCN: 文学与科学用语「绿色的」

entries.definition: of the colour of grass
growing thickly and healthily
having many leaves or being full of trees

normalIntro.en: Verdant is green in its Latin bones: virid- is the ancient word for green.
normalIntro.cn: verdant 的骨子里就是「绿」：virid- 是古代表示绿色的词根。

normal.en: Verdant hills are covered with fresh green grass.
normal.cn: verdant hills 就是长满新绿青草的山丘。

normal.en: Verdure and verdant share the Latin green root.
normal.cn: verdure 与 verdant 共享拉丁语「绿」词根。

normal.en: French vert means green, and verde is the Italian and Spanish cousin.
normal.cn: 法语 vert 意为绿色，verde 是意大利语和西班牙语的同族词。

normal.en: Verdigris is the green coat that forms on old copper.
normal.cn: verdigris 就是旧铜器上结出的绿锈。

normal.en: A verdant landscape looks bright and alive rather than dry.
normal.cn: verdant 的风景显得明亮有生气，而不是干枯的。

abstract.en: Picture a hillside washed by rain and shining with young grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一面被雨水洗过、新草发亮的山坡。

abstract.en: Imagine a garden where every leaf seems to have just unfolded.
abstract.cn: 想象一座花园，每片叶子仿佛刚刚展开。

abstract.en: Think of a young recruit whose face still has the green of youth.
abstract.cn: 想象一个新兵，脸上还带着青春的「青涩」。

examples.en: Visitors hike through verdant forests along the river.
examples.cn: 游客们沿着河流徒步穿过葱郁的森林。

examples.en: The desert turned verdant after a rare wet season.
examples.cn: 在一个罕见的雨季之后，沙漠变得绿意盎然。

examples.en: Their garden stayed verdant even in the dry summer.
examples.cn: 即使在干燥的夏天，他们的花园依然青翠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「V 额的」——发音像「V 额的」，乍看像一块绿色的「V 形山坡」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 viridis（绿色的）、virere（发绿、茂盛）→ 北部古法语 virdant → 英语 verdant，核心义「绿色、葱茏」，引申出清新与年轻；与 vert、verdure、verde 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Verdant starts from the literal colour of growing plants, then extends to freshness and vitality, and finally to young, inexperienced people.
sensesIntro.cn: verdant 从草木生长的字面绿色出发，延伸出清新与生机，最后用来形容年轻稚嫩的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rain-washed hillside of fresh green grass.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨后新绿铺满的山坡。

branches.en: Land covered in green plants is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 长满绿色植物的土地是基本义项。

branches.en: Fresh growth gives the feeling of life and energy.
branches.cn: 新生的植物带来生命力和活力的感觉。

branches.en: Green also describes an unripe, inexperienced person.
branches.cn: 绿色也用来形容尚未成熟、缺乏经验的人。

branches.en: A green field and a fresh spirit feel similar because both suggest new growth.
branches.cn: 绿色田野与清新的精神感受相似，因为两者都暗示新的生长。

branches.en: Vitality and youth meet in the idea of something still ripening.
branches.cn: 生机与年轻在「仍在成熟中」这一意象上交汇。

intro.en: Verdant is built on the Latin green family of virid-, with English relatives such as verdure, virid, and verdigris.
intro.cn: verdant 建立在拉丁语表示绿色的 virid- 词族之上，相关的英语词有 verdure、virid、verdigris。

latinIntro.en: Latin viridis means green and virere means to be green or vigorous; the family also supplies viridescent and virescent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 viridis 意为绿色，virere 意为发绿、茂盛；这一词族还衍生出 viridescent 与 virescent。

items.example: Viridis is the root meaning behind verdant.
items.exampleCN: viridis 是 verdant 的核心词根义。

items.example: Virere adds the idea of flourishing growth.
items.exampleCN: virere 增添了蓬勃生长的意味。

items.example: Old French vert gives the short colour word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 vert 提供了简短的绿色词。

items.example: The northern form virdant leads to English verdant.
items.exampleCN: 北部方言形式 virdant 通向英语 verdant。

items.example: The suffix -ant makes an adjective out of a root.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 把词根变成形容词。

items.example: Verdure is the noun of green plant growth.
items.exampleCN: verdure 是绿色草木生长的名词。

items.example: Verdigris comes from the French phrase for Greek green.
items.exampleCN: verdigris 来自法语中「希腊之绿」的说法。

items.example: Viridescent describes something becoming green.
items.exampleCN: viridescent 形容正变成绿色的东西。

items.example: Virescent young leaves appear in early spring.
items.exampleCN: 早春时长出开始泛绿的嫩叶。

items.example: Verde is the Romance cousin of verdant.
items.exampleCN: verde 是 verdant 的罗曼语同族词。

definition_zh: 边缘；路边草地；濒临；趋向；权杖
definition_en: the edge of something, especially a road or the edge of a state of affairs
core_image: 公路边一条窄窄的草带，外侧就是陡坡
scene: 暴雨下了整整两天，河水不断上涨，村里的老人家向广播求助。After two days of rain the river kept rising, and the village was on the verge of flooding.
sceneCN: 这里 verge 是「边缘、濒临」（第 2 个义项：处于某种状态的边界）；句意：雨下了两天，河水不断上涨，村庄濒临被淹。

derivatives.zh: 由 verge（权杖）+ 表人后缀 -er 构成，义为「教堂司事、执权杖者」
由前缀 con-（一起）+ 拉丁语 vergere（转向）构成，义为「汇聚；趋于一致」
由前缀 di-（分开）+ vergere 构成，义为「分叉；分歧」

senses.title: The edge of a road or area
senses.titleCN: （道路或区域的）边缘；路边草地
senses.definition: the strip of grass at the side of a road, or the edge of an area
senses.definitionCN: 道路一侧的长条草地，或某片区域的边缘
senses.example: The children played on the grassy verge beside the lane.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在车道旁长满草的边上玩耍。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin virga, a rod, and the road sense names the strip of land at the outer limit.
senses.whyCN: 该词源自拉丁语 virga（细杆），道路义指的就是位于最外边界的那一条地。

senses.title: The point just before a change
senses.definition: the point at which something is about to change or happen
senses.definitionCN: 某事物即将改变或发生的那一瞬间
senses.example: She was on the verge of quitting her job.
senses.exampleCN: 她几乎要辞掉工作了。
senses.why: Standing on an edge means one step from a new state, so the physical rim becomes a threshold in time.
senses.whyCN: 站在边缘就是离新状态只差一步，于是实体的「边」变成了时间的「临界点」。

senses.title: To be close to a condition
senses.definition: to be very close to a particular quality or state, often with verging on
senses.definitionCN: 非常接近某种性质或状态，常与 verging on 连用
senses.example: His jokes verge on cruelty.
senses.exampleCN: 他的玩笑近乎残忍。
senses.why: The verb takes the noun edge and turns it into motion: things verge on when they nearly reach it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词的「边」变成动作：事物 verge on 某处，就是几乎触到那条边。

senses.title: To move or incline toward
senses.definition: to move, bend, or tend toward something, as the older verb sense
senses.definitionCN: 旧义：向某处移动、弯曲或倾向
senses.example: The path verges toward the old mill.
senses.exampleCN: 小路朝老磨坊的方向延伸。
senses.why: Latin vergere meant to bend or turn, so the verb first described a line bending toward a point.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vergere 意为弯、转，所以动词最初描述的是一条线朝某点弯去。

senses.title: A rod carried as a symbol
senses.definition: a rod or staff held as a sign of office or authority
senses.definitionCN: 作为职位或权力象征而手持的杖
senses.example: The steward raised the verge to signal silence.
senses.exampleCN: 司仪举起权杖示意大家安静。
senses.why: The Latin source virga means a green rod or shoot, and the staff carries that original meaning.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源 virga 意为绿色细枝或嫩条，权杖义正保留着这个本义。

intro.en: Verge comes from Latin virga, a rod or green shoot, through Old French verge, and the rod sense survives in the verge carried in processions.
intro.cn: verge 来自拉丁语 virga（细杆、嫩枝），经古法语 verge 进入英语；「杖」义保存在游行中持的权杖里。

items.en: Virga means a rod, switch, or green branch, and vergere means to bend or turn.
items.cn: virga 意为细杆、枝条或绿枝；另有动词 vergere 意为弯曲、转向。

items.en: Verge carries the rod sense, and later adds the sense of a boundary strip.
items.cn: 古法语 verge 保留「杖」义，后来又增加「边界地带」之义。

items.en: In English the rod of office is recorded first; the grassy roadside sense comes later.
items.cn: 英语中先记录「权杖」义，路边的草地义出现较晚。

items.en: On the verge of comes to mean close to a change of state.
items.cn: on the verge of 开始表示接近某种状态转变。

items.en: Verge now covers roadsides, thresholds, and the verb verging on.
items.cn: 现代英语的 verge 涵盖路边、临界状态以及动词 verging on。

note.en: Verge is close in form to converge, diverge, and verger, and in meaning to edge, brink, and margin.
note.cn: verge 在形式上与 converge、diverge、verger 相近，在意义上与 edge、brink、margin 相邻。

to separate and go in different directions
