normalIntro.en: Verge is an edge word: a rod beside the road, and a line just before a change.
normalIntro.cn: verge 是个「边」字：路边的一条草地，也指变化前的那条线。

normal.en: On the verge of means very close to happening.
normal.cn: on the verge of 意为即将发生。

normal.en: Verging on means almost, as in verging on rude.
normal.cn: verging on 意为差不多、近乎，如 verging on rude。

normal.en: Converge and diverge share the Latin turning root with verge.
normal.cn: converge 与 diverge 和 verge 共享拉丁语「转向」词根。

normal.en: The grassy verge is the grass at the side of the road.
normal.cn: grassy verge 就是路边那条草地。

normal.en: A verger once carried a verge, a rod, in church processions.
normal.cn: 教堂司事在游行中曾手持权杖。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow grass strip at the edge of a motorway.
abstract.cn: 想象高速公路边缘一条窄窄的草地。

abstract.en: Imagine a cup of water filled to the very brim.
abstract.cn: 想象一只水杯已经满到杯沿。

abstract.en: Think of a road bending until it almost meets the river.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路弯过去，几乎要与河水相接。

examples.en: The country was on the verge of economic collapse.
examples.cn: 这个国家濒临经济崩溃。

examples.en: Flowers grew thickly on the verge beside the narrow road.
examples.cn: 狭窄道路旁的草地上开满了花。

examples.en: Some of his remarks verge on insult.
examples.cn: 他的一些话近乎侮辱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我急」——发音近似「我急」，站在边缘一急就会掉下去；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 virga（细杆、嫩枝）→ 古法语 verge（杖）→ 英语 verge，由「杖」引申出「边界的一条地」，再抽象为「临界点」；动词 vergere（转向）贡献了 converge、diverge 这一词族。

sensesIntro.en: Verge begins with a rod and the strip beside a road, becomes the edge of an area, and from that edge grows the idea of standing at the threshold of a change.
sensesIntro.cn: verge 从细杆和路边的一带地出发，指区域边缘，再由「边缘」长出「站在变化临界点」的含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow grass strip at the edge of a road.
core.cn: 核心意象：公路边缘的一条窄草地。

branches.en: The grass strip at the road edge is the concrete sense.
branches.cn: 路边的那条草地是具体义项。

branches.en: The edge of a state is the threshold just before change.
branches.cn: 状态的边缘就是变化前的临界点。

branches.en: Verging on turns the edge into a verb of nearness.
branches.cn: verging on 把「边」变成表示接近的动词。

branches.en: The old verb for bending toward keeps the Latin turning image.
branches.cn: 旧动词「朝某处弯曲」保留了拉丁语的转向意象。

branches.en: The ceremonial rod keeps the oldest physical meaning.
branches.cn: 仪式权杖保留着最古老的具体含义。

intro.en: Verge rests on Latin virga, a rod, and the related verb vergere, to bend, which gives converge and diverge.
intro.cn: verge 建立在拉丁语 virga（细杆）之上，相关动词 vergere（弯曲）衍生出 converge 与 diverge。

latinIntro.en: Latin virga means a rod or green branch, and vergere means to bend or turn; the two forms are close but not certainly the same word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 virga 意为细杆或绿枝，vergere 意为弯曲、转向；两种形式相近，但是否同源尚无定论。

items.example: Virga names the rod that a verge once described.
items.exampleCN: virga 指的就是 verge 曾经表示的细杆。

items.example: Vergere supplies the turning image in verge.
items.exampleCN: vergere 为 verge 提供「转向」的意象。

items.example: Verge brings both the rod and the boundary to English.
items.exampleCN: verge 把「杖」与「边界」两义带入英语。

items.example: The suffix -er forms verger from verge.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 由 verge 构成 verger。

items.example: A verger paces the aisle with a staff.
items.exampleCN: 教堂司事持杖走过过道。

items.example: Con- plus vergere forms converge.
items.exampleCN: con- 加 vergere 构成 converge。

items.example: Lines converge when they meet at a point.
items.exampleCN: 线在一点相交时就是汇聚。

items.example: Di- plus vergere forms diverge.
items.exampleCN: di- 加 vergere 构成 diverge。

items.example: Roads diverge at the fork.
items.exampleCN: 道路在岔口处分叉。

items.example: Divergent views split the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 分歧的观点让会议分裂。

definition_zh: 害虫；害兽；寄生虫；害人虫
definition_en: small animals or insects, such as rats or lice, that are harmful, dirty, or annoying, and often by extension people thought to be like them
core_image: 仓库角落里的老鼠和跳蚤，一开灯就四处乱窜
scene: 厨房里突然窜出老鼠，主人立刻打电话叫人来灭它们。When rats appeared in the kitchen, the owner called in a pest company at once to deal with the vermin.
sceneCN: 这里 vermin 是「害兽、害虫」（第 1 个义项：鼠类、昆虫等有害小动物）；句意：厨房里出现老鼠后，主人立刻请人来处理这些害兽。

pos.zh: 害虫；害兽；寄生虫（通常作集合名词，无复数形式）
害人虫；社会渣滓（引申用法，带强烈贬义）

forms.label: 复数（集合名词，形式不变）

derivatives.zh: 由名词加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，义为「满是害虫的；令人作呕的」
vermi-（蠕虫）+ -cide（杀），义为「杀肠虫药」
vermi-（蠕虫）+ -fuge（驱逐），义为「驱虫药」
拉丁语 vermiculus（小虫）加 -ar，义为「蠕虫状的」

senses.title: Small animals and insects that cause harm
senses.definition: rats, mice, insects, and other small creatures that damage property, spread disease, or spoil food
senses.definitionCN: 老鼠、昆虫等会破坏财物、传播疾病或糟蹋食物的小动物
senses.example: The old barn was full of vermin.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧谷仓里到处都是老鼠害虫。
senses.why: Latin vermis means a worm, and in English the word first covered all crawling creatures before narrowing to the ones people want gone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vermis 本指「虫」，英语里先泛指各种爬行小虫，后来缩小到人们想除掉的害虫害兽。

senses.title: Parasites living on people or animals
senses.definition: tiny creatures such as lice or fleas that live on people or animals and feed on them
senses.definitionCN: 虱子、跳蚤等寄生在人畜身上、以人畜为食的小生物
senses.example: Prisoners suffered from vermin in their clothes.
senses.exampleCN: 囚犯们的衣服里生了虱子。
senses.why: Since worms and lice were the oldest tiny pests, the word keeps a special place for parasites that live outside or inside a body.
senses.whyCN: 虫和虱子是最古老的微型害物，所以这个词一直保留「寄生在人畜身上的小生物」这一层。

senses.title: People seen as disgusting or harmful
senses.definition: people who are considered disgusting, worthless, or a danger to others, used as strong abuse
senses.definitionCN: 被认为可憎、无用或对他人有害的人，用作强烈的辱骂
senses.example: The old newspapers called the thieves vermin.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的报纸把这些窃贼称作人渣。
senses.why: The move from pests to people is metaphor: anyone treated like a rat in the corner is named with a word for rats.
senses.whyCN: 从害虫到人是隐喻转移：被当成角落里老鼠对待的人，就用称呼老鼠的词来叫。

senses.title: Wild animals treated as pests
senses.definition: wild animals such as foxes or pigeons that are officially classed as troublesome in a place
senses.definitionCN: 狐狸、鸽子等在某一地区被官方列为有害的野生动物
senses.example: Under the law, foxes count as vermin on this farm.
senses.exampleCN: 按照法律，狐狸在这座农场算有害动物。
senses.why: Farming and hunting laws extend the pest idea from small creatures to larger wild animals that harm crops or livestock.
senses.whyCN: 农业和狩猎法规把「害虫」的概念从小生物扩展到危害庄稼或牲畜的较大野生动物。

senses.title: A group of pests, taken together
senses.definition: a number of such harmful creatures regarded as one mass to be controlled or removed
senses.definitionCN: 将许多有害生物视为一个整体，需要控制或清除
senses.example: Restaurants must keep vermin out of the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 餐馆必须避免厨房里出现老鼠虫类。
senses.why: Vermin is a collection noun like cattle or police, so it names the whole swarm rather than one animal.
senses.whyCN: vermin 像 cattle 或 police 一样是集合名词，所以它指一整群，而不是单独一只。

senses.title: Crawling things seen with disgust
senses.definition: creepy crawling creatures that provoke fear or disgust rather than direct damage
senses.definitionCN: 让人害怕或恶心、未必直接造成损害的爬行小生物
senses.example: She is frightened of every kind of vermin.
senses.exampleCN: 她对任何虫子都感到害怕。
senses.why: The worm image at the core explains why the feeling of crawling and disgust sits so close to the word.
senses.whyCN: 核心的「虫子」意象解释了为什么这个词总与爬行感和厌恶感相伴。

senses.title: Harmful computer programs
senses.definition: malicious software or programs that spread and damage a computer system
senses.definitionCN: 在电脑系统中扩散并造成破坏的恶意软件或程序
senses.example: The antivirus program removed the vermin overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 杀毒程序一夜之间清掉了这些有害程序。
senses.why: Computing borrows the pest image for programs that infest a system, multiply, and must be exterminated.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用害虫意象来形容那些寄居系统、不断繁殖、必须清除掉的有害程序。

intro.en: Vermin goes back to Latin vermis, a worm, and came into English from French forms of the same word.
intro.cn: vermin 可追溯到拉丁语 vermis（虫），经由同一词根的法语词形进入英语。

items.en: Vermis means a worm or a crawling grub.
items.cn: vermis 意为虫、蠕虫或幼虫。

items.en: A noun built on vermis comes to name any crawling creature.
items.cn: 由 vermis 构成的名称逐渐泛指各种爬行小生物。

items.en: French vermine speaks of small noxious animals.
items.cn: 法语 vermine 指有害的小动物。

items.en: Vermin enters English and first covers worms and crawling insects.
items.cn: vermin 进入英语，起初兼指蠕虫与爬行昆虫。

items.en: The sense narrows to rats, mice, and other pests around houses and farms.
items.cn: 词义收窄到房屋和农场周围的老鼠等害兽。

items.en: The word is used for despised people and later for harmful software.
items.cn: 这个词被用来指受鄙视的人，后来又用于有害软件。

note.en: Vermin sits with the worm-root family vermis and verminous, and next to everyday pest and rodent words.
note.cn: vermin 属于「虫」词根家族，与 vermis、verminous 同源，并与 pest、rodent 等日常词相邻。

entries.definition: full of pests or parasites
a medicine that kills intestinal worms
shaped like a worm
an insect or animal that harms crops, food, or health
a gnawing animal such as a rat or mouse
a creature that lives on another and feeds from it

normalIntro.en: Vermin is the worm-root word: small crawling creatures that people want gone.
normalIntro.cn: vermin 是「虫子」词根词：指人们想赶走的小型爬行生物。

normal.en: Vermin is a collection noun, so we say the vermin is destroyed, not vermins.
normal.cn: vermin 是集合名词，所以要说害虫被消灭，而不用复数形式。

normal.en: Verminous adds the -ous suffix to mean full of pests.
normal.cn: verminous 加形容词后缀 -ous，义为「满是害虫的」。

normal.en: Vermicide uses the same root as suicide, sci or cide meaning to cut down.
normal.cn: vermicide 与 suicide 同用词根，意为「杀死」。

normal.en: Farmers speak of vermin control, just as they speak of pest control.
normal.cn: 农场主说 vermin control，就像说 pest control 一样。

normal.en: Like pest, vermin belongs to housing, health, and farming texts.
normal.cn: 和 pest 一样，vermin 常见于住房、卫生和农业文本。

abstract.en: Picture rats racing along a warehouse beam when the light flicks on.
abstract.cn: 想象灯一亮，老鼠沿着仓库横梁四处逃窜。

abstract.en: Picture lice climbing inside a worn winter coat.
abstract.cn: 想象虱子爬进一件破旧冬衣的内衬。

abstract.en: Picture a gardener pointing at moles and calling them pests with one word.
abstract.cn: 想象园丁指着鼹鼠，用一个词把它们统称为害兽。

examples.en: Vermin were getting into the grain store every night.
examples.cn: 害虫害兽每晚都钻进粮仓。

examples.en: The health inspector found the restaurant infested with vermin.
examples.cn: 卫生检查员发现这家餐馆有鼠虫侵扰。

examples.en: Propaganda often calls enemies vermin in order to justify cruelty.
examples.cn: 宣传常把敌人称作人渣，以给残酷行为找理由。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「窝门」——害虫从窝门口成群钻进厨房；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vermis（虫、蠕虫）→ 拉丁语晚期依此构成泛指爬虫的词 → 古法语 vermine → 英语 vermin，核心义「成群的小害物」。

sensesIntro.en: Vermin starts from the worm and crawls outward: pests, parasites, despised people, and finally harmful programs.
sensesIntro.cn: vermin 从「虫」出发一路延伸：害虫害兽、寄生虫、人渣，最后是有害程序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rats and fleas swarming in a corner that people want cleared.
core.cn: 核心意象：老鼠和跳蚤在角落里成群，人们恨不得彻底清除。

branches.en: Rats and insects that spoil food or property are the core sense.
branches.cn: 糟蹋食物毁坏财物的鼠类昆虫是核心义。

branches.en: Parasites on bodies keep the old worm image closest to the surface.
branches.cn: 身上的寄生虫最贴近古老的「虫」意象。

branches.en: Calling people vermin is metaphor built on disgust.
branches.cn: 把人称作人渣，是建立在厌恶之上的隐喻。

branches.en: Wild animals classed as pests and whole swarms both widen the word to groups.
branches.cn: 被列为有害的野生动物与成群的害虫害兽，都把这个词扩展到群体。

branches.en: Crawling disgust and malicious software both reuse the pest image.
branches.cn: 爬虫引起的恶心感与恶意软件，都复用了害虫意象。

intro.en: Vermin is built on the worm root vermi-, which also shapes verminous, vermicide, and vermicular.
intro.cn: vermin 建立在「虫」词根 vermi- 之上，verminous、vermicide、vermicular 也都由它构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin vermis means a worm, and its diminutive vermiculus means a little worm.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vermis 意为虫，其指小形式 vermiculus 意为小虫。

items.example: Vermis is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: vermis 是整个词族的根源。

items.example: The small worm gives vermicular its shape idea.
items.exampleCN: 「小虫」这一层给了 vermicular 形状上的含义。

items.example: Vermin names the pests as a group.
items.exampleCN: vermin 作为整体指害虫害兽。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms verminous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 verminous。

items.example: Verminous describes a filthy infested place.
items.exampleCN: verminous 形容布满害虫的肮脏之处。

items.example: Vermi- opens medical words about worms.
items.exampleCN: vermi- 构成关于蠕虫的医学词。

items.example: The suffix -cide forms vermicide.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -cide 构成 vermicide。

items.example: Vermicide kills worms inside the body.
items.exampleCN: vermicide 杀灭体内的虫。

items.example: The suffix -fuge forms vermifuge.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -fuge 构成 vermifuge。

items.example: Vermicular keeps the little-worm image.
items.exampleCN: vermicular 保留「小虫」的意象。

definition_zh: 本地话；方言；白话；土语；本民族语；白话的；本地风格的
definition_en: the language or dialect that ordinary people in a particular place or group speak, and by extension the ordinary style of a field instead of its formal or technical one
core_image: 乡村集市的土话声：老人用自家方言讨价还价
scene: 在山区旅行时，向导用当地土话跟老农交谈，游客一句也听不懂。While hiking in the mountains, the guide talked to an old farmer in the local vernacular, and the tourists understood nothing.
sceneCN: 这里 vernacular 是「本地话、方言」（第 1 个义项：一个地方普通人的日常口语）；句意：在山里徒步时，向导用当地方言与老农交谈，游客完全听不懂。

pos.zh: 本地话；方言；白话；土语（常作 the vernacular）
白话的；本地话的；地方风格的

collocations.zh: 乡土建筑（本地风格建筑）

derivatives.zh: 由名词加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使白话化；译成本地话」
名词加 -ism 构成，义为「方言表达；土语用法」
形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「用白话地；以本地风格地」

senses.title: The everyday speech of a place
senses.definition: the native language or dialect spoken by ordinary people in a particular region
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区普通百姓日常使用的本族语或方言
senses.example: Elderly villagers still speak the old vernacular.
senses.exampleCN: 年长的村民仍讲着老的方言。
senses.why: Latin verna means a slave born in the household, so vernacular is the speech of the home-born rather than of outsiders.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 verna 指「生在家里的奴隶」，所以 vernacular 指「土生土长的人」的话，而不是外来者的话。

senses.title: Ordinary speech opposed to formal Latin
senses.definition: the common language of a country as opposed to Latin or another learned language used for writing
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家的通用口语，与用于写作的拉丁文或学术语言相对
senses.example: Early writers translated the Bible into the vernacular.
senses.exampleCN: 早期作家把《圣经》译成白话。
senses.why: For centuries scholars wrote in Latin, so the vernacular came to mean the common tongue standing against the learned one.
senses.whyCN: 几百年来学者都用拉丁文写作，于是 vernacular 逐渐指与学术语言相对的普通白话。

senses.title: The grammar and words of a specific group
senses.definition: the particular speech patterns shared by a named group, region, or social community
senses.definitionCN: 某一有名群体、地区或社会共同体共有的特定说话方式
senses.example: Linguists study the vernacular of this island community.
senses.exampleCN: 语言学家研究这个岛屿社群的方言。
senses.why: If home speech defines a community, then naming any community lets the word name their shared way of talking.
senses.whyCN: 如果家乡话定义了一个社群，那么任何社群共有的说话方式都可以用这个词来称呼。

senses.title: Local style in building or craft
senses.definition: the traditional style of building or making things that grows from local materials and habits
senses.definitionCN: 由本地材料和习惯发展出的传统建筑或制作风格
senses.example: The village houses show a strong vernacular style.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的房屋显露出鲜明的乡土风格。
senses.why: The idea of home-grown speech stretches to home-grown design, so buildings made by local makers in local ways are called vernacular too.
senses.whyCN: 「土生土长的语言」这一想法延伸到土生土长的设计，于是本地匠人用本地方式造的房子也叫 vernacular。

senses.title: The informal jargon of a profession
senses.definition: the plain working language that people in a field use among themselves instead of official terms
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域的人在内部使用、而非用正式术语的通俗工作语言
senses.example: Ask any vet what the vernacular of their clinic is like.
senses.exampleCN: 问任何兽医，诊所里的行话是什么样。
senses.why: Just as scholars once had Latin and the people had the vernacular, each profession has official terms and a plain inner speech.
senses.whyCN: 正如学者有拉丁文、百姓有白话，每个行业也都有正式术语与内部通俗说法。

senses.title: Plain and homely in tone
senses.definition: describing a style that is plain, ordinary, and close to everyday speech rather than refined
senses.definitionCN: 形容文风朴素、日常，接近口语而非精致典雅
senses.example: His letters were deliberately vernacular and warm.
senses.exampleCN: 他的书信刻意写得通俗而亲切。
senses.why: Judgement sticks to the word: what is close to home speech can be praised as natural or dismissed as unrefined.
senses.whyCN: 评价色彩附着在这个词上：接近家乡话既可以称赞为自然，也可以贬为不精致。

senses.title: The name of a plant or animal in local speech
senses.definition: the local everyday name for a plant, animal, or thing, as opposed to its scientific name
senses.definitionCN: 动植物或事物在当地俗称的名字，与学名相对
senses.example: The vernacular for this plant is as harmless as it sounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物的俗名听起来就像它本身一样无害。
senses.why: Scientific names are international Latin, so the local folk name is by definition the vernacular one.
senses.whyCN: 学名是国际通用的拉丁语，所以当地的民间叫法按定义就是 vernacular。

intro.en: Vernacular comes from Latin vernaculus, meaning native or household, built on verna, a slave born in the house.
intro.cn: vernacular 来自拉丁语 vernaculus（本地的、家中的），其词根 verna 指「生在家里的奴隶」。

items.en: Verna names a slave born in the household rather than bought.
items.cn: verna 指生在家中、而非买来的奴隶。

items.en: The adjective vernaculus means belonging to the household or native to a place.
items.cn: 形容词 vernaculus 意为「家里的」或「本地的」。

items.en: Writers use vernacula to name the speech of home-born people, opposing it to Latin.
items.cn: 写作者用 vernacula 指土生土长的人们说的话，与拉丁文相对。

items.en: Vernacular enters English as a name for the native or ordinary language.
items.cn: 十七世纪，vernacular 进入英语，指本族语或普通语言。

items.en: Architecture and craft writing borrow it for local traditional styles.
items.cn: 建筑与工艺写作借用它指本地传统风格。

items.en: Linguistics keeps the word for regional, social, and professional speech varieties.
items.cn: 现代语言学用它指地区、社会与行业的不同语言变体。

note.en: Vernacular connects to the home-born root verna and sits beside dialect, slang, and colloquial words.
note.cn: vernacular 与「生在家中」的词根 verna 相连，并与 dialect、slang、colloquial 等词相邻。

entries.definition: a word or phrase from the local speech
entries.definitionCN: 来自本地话的词语或说法

entries.definition: to put into the local language
belonging to spring
entries.definitionCN: 春天的（只是拼写相近，词源不同，源于拉丁语 ver）

entries.definition: a form of a language used in one region or group
suitable for ordinary conversation
very informal words used by a particular group

normalIntro.en: Vernacular is the speech born in the house: what locals say when nobody is writing in Latin.
normalIntro.cn: vernacular 是「生在家里的语言」：没人用拉丁文写作时，本地人日常说的话。

normal.en: The root verna, a home-born slave, explains why the word means native and homely.
normal.cn: 词根 verna 指家生奴隶，这解释了为什么这个词有「本地的、家常的」之意。

normal.en: In the vernacular is the usual fixed phrase for saying something in plain local words.
normal.cn: in the vernacular 是固定说法，表示「用白话讲」。

normal.en: History texts pair vernacular with Latin: the vernacular Bible against the Latin one.
normal.cn: 历史文本把 vernacular 与拉丁文对举：白话圣经对拉丁文圣经。

normal.en: Vernacular architecture means buildings made from local materials by local builders.
normal.cn: vernacular architecture 指本地匠人用本地材料建成的房屋。

normal.en: Compare dialect: dialect is the regional form, vernacular stresses everyday use by ordinary people.
normal.cn: 对比 dialect：dialect 强调地区形态，vernacular 强调普通人日常使用。

abstract.en: Picture a village market where every vendor speaks a different local accent.
abstract.cn: 想象一个乡村集市，每个摊主都带着不同的本地口音。

abstract.en: Picture a monk reading Latin aloud while a farmer answers in his home tongue.
abstract.cn: 想象修士高声读拉丁文，而农夫用家乡话回答。

abstract.en: Picture a farmhouse built of local stone and straw, no architect needed.
abstract.cn: 想象一座用本地石头和稻草搭起来的农舍，不需要建筑师。

examples.en: For two hundred years, the vernacular replaced Latin in court papers.
examples.cn: 两百年间，白话取代拉丁文成为法庭文件的用语。

examples.en: The novel is written in the vernacular of the fishing villages.
examples.cn: 这部小说用渔村的本地方言写成。

examples.en: Doctors have their own vernacular, and patients often misread it.
examples.cn: 医生有自己的一套行话，病人常常误解。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我拿腔克勒」——本地人故意拿腔拿调逗外乡人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 verna（家生的奴隶）→ vernaculus（家里的、本地的）→ 拉丁语写作中的 vernacula（本族语）→ 英语 vernacular，核心义「土生土长的语言」。

sensesIntro.en: From home-born speech, vernacular widens into the language of a group, its local style, and the plain inner jargon of a field.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「家里生出来的话」出发，vernacular 扩展为群体语言、本地风格，以及某一行业的内部白话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sound of a home town dialect in a busy local market.
core.cn: 核心意象：热闹的本地集市上，家乡方言的声音。

branches.en: Everyday regional speech is the central sense.
branches.cn: 地区日常口语是中心义项。

branches.en: The contrast with Latin makes vernacular a written as well as spoken label.
branches.cn: 与拉丁文的对立让 vernacular 既能指口语也能指书面语。

branches.en: Naming a community turns the word into the speech of a group.
branches.cn: 点明某个社群，这个词就变成某群体的语言。

branches.en: Home-grown building and plain style both borrow the home idea.
branches.cn: 乡土建筑与朴素文风都借用了「家」的意味。

branches.en: Trade jargon and folk names are the local speech of professions and nature.
branches.cn: 行话与俗名分别是行业与自然的「本地话」。

intro.en: Vernacular is built on the Latin home root verna, and English extends it with -ize, -ism, and -ly.
intro.cn: vernacular 建立在拉丁语「家」词根 verna 之上，英语再用 -ize、-ism、-ly 加以扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin verna means a home-born slave, and vernaculus means native or belonging to the household.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 verna 意为家生奴隶，vernaculus 意为本地的或属于家中的。

items.meaning: a slave born in the house
items.example: Verna gives the word its born-here sense.
items.exampleCN: verna 赋予这个词「生在此地」的含义。

items.example: Vernaculus is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: vernaculus 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: Vernacular keeps the home-grown meaning.
items.exampleCN: vernacular 保留了「土生土长」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ar shapes the Latin adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ar 构成这个拉丁语形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms vernacularize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 vernacularize。

items.meaning: to translate into the local language
items.example: Vernacularize means to put a text into plain local words.
items.exampleCN: vernacularize 指把文本译成本地白话。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms vernacularism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 vernacularism。

items.example: Vernacularism names one piece of local speech.
items.exampleCN: vernacularism 指一条具体的土语说法。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb vernacularly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 vernacularly。

items.example: Vernacularly means in the manner of plain local speech.
items.exampleCN: vernacularly 表示「以平实本地话的方式」。

definition_zh: 对；与……相对；对抗；诉（某人）；与……相比
definition_en: used to show that two people, sides, ideas, or choices are being compared, opposed, or played against each other
core_image: 球场上两队隔着中线面对面站好，裁判指向中间
scene: 赛程表上写着今晚两支球队的队名，中间隔着一个小小的对字。The schedule shows the two team names side by side, with a small versus between them.
sceneCN: 这里 versus 是「对、对抗」（第 1 个义项：表示比赛双方对立）；句意：赛程表上两个队名并排写着，中间有一个小小的对字。

pos.zh: 对；与……相对；对抗；与……相比（常缩写作 v）
诉（某人）（法律用语，如 A versus B）

derivatives.zh: 由同源拉丁语 adversarius（对面的人）构成，义为「对手；敌方」
同源于拉丁语 adversus（转向对面的），义为「不利的；相反的」
re-（向后）+ vers（转向），义为「反转；倒退」
con-（一起）+ vers（转向），义为「转换；改变」

senses.title: Opposing teams in a contest
senses.definition: used between the names of two teams or players to show who is playing against whom
senses.definitionCN: 放在两队或两名选手的名字之间，表示谁与谁对阵
senses.example: The final is United versus City.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛是联队对城队。
senses.why: Latin versus is the old participle of vertere, to turn, so versus names two sides turned to face each other.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 versus 是 vertere（转向）的旧分词，所以 versus 指双方转过身面对面。

senses.title: Two sides turned against each other
senses.definition: used between opposing people, armies, or groups outside formal sport
senses.definitionCN: 用于体育之外的对立双方，如对手、军队或群体之间
senses.example: The press keeps pitching the minister versus the board.
senses.exampleCN: 媒体一直把部长与董事会描写成对立双方。
senses.why: The same facing image expands from the pitch to any dispute where two camps stand opposed.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「面对面」的意象从球场扩展到任何两派对立的情形。

senses.title: A choice weighed against another
senses.definition: used between two possibilities or amounts to compare their pros, cons, or costs
senses.definitionCN: 放在两种可能或两个数量之间，比较优劣或代价
senses.example: We must weigh quality versus cost.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须权衡质量与成本。
senses.why: When two options are set face to face, one must be judged against the other, so facing becomes comparing.
senses.whyCN: 当两个选项面对面摆在一起时，总要一个对另一个做判断，于是「面对面」就变成了「比较」。

senses.title: One idea set against another
senses.definition: used to set two ideas, views, or statements side by side as contrasts
senses.definitionCN: 把两种观念、看法或说法并置，表明其对立
senses.example: The essay contrasts tradition versus change.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把传统与变革相对照。
senses.why: Abstract ideas can also be pictured as two sides facing off, so the word also frames contrasts in argument.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的观点也能被想象成面对面的两方，所以这个词也用于论证中的对照。

senses.title: Party against party in a lawsuit
senses.definition: used in case names between the party bringing the action and the party defending it
senses.definitionCN: 用于案名中，连接起诉方与被诉方
senses.example: The famous case Smith versus Jones changed the law.
senses.exampleCN: 著名的史密斯诉琼斯案改变了法律。
senses.why: Courtroom cases are literally two parties turned to face each other before a judge.
senses.whyCN: 法庭案件本来就是双方在法官面前转过身相对，所以 versus 进入了案名。

senses.title: A figure matched against another
senses.definition: used between two figures, percentages, or results to show which is larger or better
senses.definitionCN: 用于两个数字、百分比或结果之间，显示谁更大或更好
senses.example: Sales rose twenty per cent versus last year.
senses.exampleCN: 销售额与去年相比增长了百分之二十。
senses.why: Statistics borrow the sports scoreboard: two numbers face each other across the word.
senses.whyCN: 统计数据借用了体育记分牌：两个数字隔着一个 versus 相对。

senses.title: In the short written form
senses.definition: the abbreviated form used in headlines, schedules, and legal tables for the same meanings
senses.definitionCN: 标题、赛程和法律表格中使用的缩写形式，含义相同
senses.example: Check the vs column before you bet.
senses.exampleCN: 下注之前先看看对战那一栏。
senses.why: A long Latin word on a scoreboard shrinks to two letters, yet the facing image stays.
senses.whyCN: 记分牌上放不下长长的拉丁词，就缩成两个字母，但「面对面」的意象仍在。

intro.en: Versus is a Latin word kept unchanged in English: it is the old form of the participle of vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: versus 是不加改动直接借用的拉丁语词：它是动词 vertere（转向）分词的旧形式。

items.en: The root wer- means to turn or bend, and lies behind the family.
items.cn: 词根 wer- 意为「转、弯」，是这一词族的远源。

items.en: Vertere means to turn, and its participle versus means turned toward.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 意为转，其分词 versus 意为「转向……的」。

items.en: In Roman law the pattern A versus B names two parties facing each other.
items.cn: 罗马法律中甲对乙的写法，指相互面对的两方。

items.en: English adopts versus in legal case names first.
items.cn: 英语先在法律案名中采用 versus。

items.en: Sporting reports make versus the standard marker between two teams.
items.cn: 体育报道让 versus 成为两队对阵的固定标记。

items.en: The abbreviation vs spreads through headlines, statistics, and everyday comparison.
items.cn: 缩写 vs 遍布标题、统计和日常比较。

note.en: Versus shares the turning root vers with adverse, reverse, and convert, and sits beside against, opposite, and compare.
note.cn: versus 与 adverse、reverse、convert 共享「转」词根 vers，并与 against、opposite、compare 等词相邻。

entries.definition: unfavourable or turned against
to turn something the other way
the opposite of a statement
in opposition to
facing across from something
to judge two things by their differences

normalIntro.en: Versus is the turning word: two sides turn to face each other before they fight, compare, or argue.
normalIntro.cn: versus 是「转」词：两方转过身面对面，然后比赛、比较或争辩。

normal.en: Versus keeps the Latin vers shape found in reverse and adverse.
normal.cn: versus 保留拉丁词形 vers，在 reverse 和 adverse 里都能见到。

normal.en: In sport and law the full word is preferred, while vs is used in headlines and scores.
normal.cn: 体育和法律多用完整形式，vs 则用于标题和比分。

normal.en: Versus joins two equal items, so write team A versus team B, not team A versus itself.
normal.cn: versus 连接两个对等项，所以写甲队对乙队，而非自己对自己。

normal.en: The phrase weigh one option versus another is common in essays.
normal.cn: essays 中常见 weigh one option versus another 这类说法。

normal.en: Compare with: versus often marks opposition, while with usually means together.
normal.cn: 对比 with：versus 常表示对立，而 with 通常表示一起。

abstract.en: Picture two boxers touching gloves across a short line.
abstract.cn: 想象两名拳手隔着一条短线碰拳。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom where two lawyers sit on opposite tables.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭里两名律师坐在相对的两张桌后。

abstract.en: Picture a shopping list with price versus quality written by the same hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张购物清单，同一个人的笔迹写下价格对质量。

examples.en: Tonight match is Germany versus Brazil.
examples.cn: 今晚的比赛是德国对巴西。

examples.en: Using a bike versus driving saves money but takes time.
examples.cn: 骑车相比于开车省钱，但更花时间。

examples.en: In the history of the civil rights movement, Brown versus the Board of Education is a turning point.
examples.cn: 在民权运动史上，布朗诉教育委员会案是一个转折点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我色死」——球场上两队互不服气，谁也不让；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 印欧词根 wer-（转）→ 拉丁语 vertere（转向）→ 分词 versus（转向……的、面对……的）→ 英语 versus，核心义「面对面」。

sensesIntro.en: Versus starts from two sides turned face to face, then branches into contest, opposition, comparison, law, and statistics.
sensesIntro.cn: versus 从「两方相对而立」出发，再分出比赛、对抗、比较、法律和统计等义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two teams standing face to face across a centre line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两支队伍隔着中线面对面站好。

branches.en: Team against team is the most familiar sense.
branches.cn: 队队对阵是最熟悉的义项。

branches.en: Hostile pairs and opposed ideas share the facing frame.
branches.cn: 敌对的双方与对立的思想共用「面对面」的框架。

branches.en: Contests and comparisons both set two equal items against each other.
branches.cn: 比赛与比较都是把两个对等的项摆到一起。

branches.en: Opposed ideas, legal parties, and statistics all reuse the opposition frame.
branches.cn: 对立的观点、诉讼双方和统计数字都复用了对立框架。

branches.en: The short form keeps the same opposition on schedules and scoreboards.
branches.cn: 缩写形式在赛程表和记分牌上保留同样的对立关系。

intro.en: Versus is a Latin form kept whole, and the turning root vers also shapes adverse, reverse, and convert.
intro.cn: versus 是整体保留的拉丁词形，「转」词根 vers 还构成 adverse、reverse、convert。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere means to turn, and versus is its older participle form meaning turned toward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 意为转，versus 是其较旧的分词形式，意为「转向……的」。

items.example: The root wer- lies behind many turning words.
items.exampleCN: 词根 wer- 隐藏在众多表示「转」的词之后。

items.example: Vertere is the verb under versus.
items.exampleCN: vertere 是 versus 底下的动词。

items.example: Versus pictured two sides facing each other.
items.exampleCN: versus 描绘两方互相面对。

items.example: The prefix ad- plus vers gives adverse.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ad- 加 vers 构成 adverse。

items.example: Adverse weather delays flights.
items.exampleCN: adverse weather 指不利天气会延误航班。

items.example: Adversary came from a Latin word for the person opposite.
items.exampleCN: adversary 来自拉丁语中表示「对面的人」的词。

items.example: The prefix re- plus vers gives reverse.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 加 vers 构成 reverse。

items.example: Reverse the car slowly.
items.exampleCN: 慢慢倒车。

items.example: The prefix con- plus vers gives convert.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 con- 加 vers 构成 convert。

items.example: Convert data into charts for the report.
items.exampleCN: 把数据转换成图表用于报告。

definition_zh: 垂直地；竖直地；纵向地；按照从上到下或从下到上的方向
definition_en: in a line that goes straight up and down, or along the up-and-down axis of something
core_image: 一根笔直竖立的木杆，从上到下与地面成直角
scene: 工地上，工人把一根长木杆立起来，用水平仪一点点校准。They fixed the pole so that it stood perfectly vertically.
sceneCN: 这里 vertically 是「垂直地、竖直地」（第 1 个义项：沿竖直方向笔直立起）；句意：他们把木杆固定好，让它完全垂直地立着。

derivatives.zh: 由副词去掉词尾构成形容词，义为「垂直的；竖直的」
在垂直之上再加名词后缀构成，义为「垂直性」
同一词形也可作名词，义为「垂直线；竖直位置」

senses.title: In an up and down line
senses.definition: in a straight line that goes up and down and meets the horizon at a right angle
senses.definitionCN: 沿一条上下延伸、与地平线成直角的直线
senses.example: Hang the picture vertically so that it matches the door frame.
senses.exampleCN: 把画竖直挂好，让它和门框对齐。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the adjective sense of following the vertical line, a line that runs straight up and down.
senses.whyCN: 副词保留形容词「沿竖直线」的含义，也就是沿一条上下笔直的线展开。

senses.title: At right angles to the ground
senses.definition: standing or rising at a right angle to the level surface beneath it
senses.definitionCN: 相对下方水平面以直角立起或上升
senses.example: The rocket rose vertically before it began to turn east.
senses.exampleCN: 火箭先垂直上升，然后开始转向东方。
senses.why: A plumb line is held up against the ground, so vertical also means square to the flat surface, not just towards the sky.
senses.whyCN: 铅垂线是相对地面竖直拉起的，所以 vertical 不只是朝向天空，还强调与水平面构成直角。

senses.title: Along the lengthwise or depthwise axis
senses.definition: along the axis that runs from end to end or from top to bottom of a shape
senses.definitionCN: 沿一个形状从一端到另一端、或从上到下的轴线
senses.example: Fold the sheet vertically so that the short edges meet.
senses.exampleCN: 把纸纵向对折，让两条短边对齐。
senses.why: Once vertical names the long axis rather than the level direction, the adverb can describe layout, folding, and grading along that axis.
senses.whyCN: 当 vertical 指的不是水平方向而是物体自身的长轴时，副词就能描述沿这一长轴的排版、折叠与分级。

senses.title: In an organisational chain from top to bottom
senses.definition: within an organisation or industry, from the top level down to the bottom level, or from one stage to an earlier or later one
senses.definitionCN: 在组织或行业内部，从最高层向下直达最底层，或从一个环节延伸到上游或下游环节
senses.example: The group is vertically integrated, from the farm to the shop shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 这个集团实现了纵向一体化，从农场一直做到商店货架。
senses.why: The up and down picture of a ladder becomes a metaphor for levels of authority or stages of production joined in a chain.
senses.whyCN: 竖直的梯子图景被用来比喻上下相连的职权层级或生产环节，于是一个物理方向变成组织与行业的纵向链条。

senses.title: Straight up into the air
senses.definition: moving or directing something straight upwards rather than at a slant
senses.definitionCN: 沿正上方移动，或把某物径直向上送出，而不是斜着送出
senses.example: The pilot pulled back the handle, and the plane climbed vertically.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员拉杆，飞机垂直爬升。
senses.why: Because the vertical line includes both ends, the adverb covers not only standing upright but also launching and climbing straight up.
senses.whyCN: 因为竖直线包含上下两端，副词既覆盖稳稳立起，也覆盖径直向上发射与爬升的情形。

senses.title: In a column layout
senses.definition: arranged in a column, so that items sit one above another rather than side by side
senses.definitionCN: 排列成竖列，使条目上下相叠而不是左右并列
senses.example: List the names vertically, one under another.
senses.exampleCN: 把名字排成竖列，一个写在另一个下面。
senses.why: On a page or a screen the vertical direction is the column direction, so the adverb also describes how text and data are stacked.
senses.whyCN: 在纸面或屏幕上，竖直方向就是列的排布方向，于是副词也能描述文字与数据如何上下堆叠。

senses.title: Across all levels of size or rank
senses.definition: covering a whole range from small to large or from low to high within a system
senses.definitionCN: 在一个体系内覆盖从小到大或从低到高的整段范围
senses.example: Wind speeds were compared vertically through the cloud layer.
senses.exampleCN: 风速在云层中被逐层从下到上作了比较。
senses.why: A vertical cut through a stack passes through every layer in turn, which gives the extended sense of covering a whole range of levels.
senses.whyCN: 对一叠层状物作竖直切面会依次穿过每一层，于是引申出「覆盖整段层级」的用法。

senses.title: Learning and printing in upright form
senses.definition: written or printed in a top-to-bottom direction, as in some upright scripts and old printing styles
senses.definitionCN: 沿从上到下的方向书写或印刷，见于部分竖写文字与旧式印刷
senses.example: The old sign was painted vertically, in tall narrow characters.
senses.exampleCN: 那块旧招牌是竖着写的，字又高又窄。
senses.why: Scripts that run down the page follow the vertical line, so the adverb marks a writing or printing style rather than a physical angle.
senses.whyCN: 文字顺着页面向下书写，走的就是竖直线，所以这个副词也可标记一种书写或印刷样式，而不是物理角度。

intro.en: Vertically is built from vertical and the adverb suffix, and vertical comes from Latin vertex, the spinning point at the top of the head.
intro.cn: vertically 由 vertical 加副词后缀构成，而 vertical 来自拉丁语 vertex，指头顶飞旋的那个点。

items.en: Vertex means a whirl, a peak, or the crown of the head, from vertere, to turn.
items.cn: vertex 意为旋涡、顶点或头顶，源自 vertere（转动）。

items.en: In late Latin, verticalis is used for the point straight above the head.
items.cn: 在晚期拉丁语中，verticalis 用来指头顶正上方的那一点。

items.en: English borrows verticalis as vertical, first for the top of the head and then for a line straight up.
items.cn: 英语借入 verticalis 写作 vertical，最初指头顶，继而指笔直向上的线。

items.en: Vertical is used in astronomy and building for lines that point to the zenith.
items.cn: vertical 在天文学与建筑中用于表示指向天顶的线。

items.en: The adverb vertically appears beside the adjective for manner and direction.
items.cn: 副词 vertically 与形容词并用，表示方式与方向。

items.en: Vertical and vertically extend to charts, printing, and business structures.
items.cn: vertical 与 vertically 扩展到图表、印刷与商业结构等领域。

note.en: Vertically belongs to the vertical word family and sits near upright, perpendicular, and plumb.
note.cn: vertically 属于 vertical 词族，并与 upright、perpendicular、plumb 近义。

entries.definition: going straight up and down
the quality of standing straight up
the highest point, or a corner of a shape
standing in a vertical position
at an angle of ninety degrees to a surface or line
exactly vertical, as checked with a weighted line

normalIntro.en: Vertically keeps the vertical family together: the adverb, the adjective, the noun, and the Latin ancestor vertex all point to one upright line.
normalIntro.cn: vertically 把 vertical 词族连在一起：副词、形容词、名词以及拉丁语祖先 vertex 都指向同一条竖直线。

normal.en: Add the adverb suffix to vertical and you get vertically.
normal.cn: 在 vertical 后加副词后缀就得到 vertically。

normal.en: Draw vertically means along the up and down direction on the page.
normal.cn: 「draw vertically」表示沿纸面上下方向画。

normal.en: A plumb line hangs vertically because of gravity.
normal.cn: 记住铅垂测试：铅垂线因重力而竖直垂下。

normal.en: A vertically integrated company owns the whole chain from source to shop.
normal.cn: 纵向一体化的公司掌控从源头到商店的整条链条。

normal.en: The Latin vertex means a turning point on top, which is why the top of the head and a vertical axis share a word.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 vertex 意为顶端的旋点，所以头顶与竖直轴共用同一个词。

abstract.en: Picture a taut string with a weight at the bottom, hanging perfectly straight.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绷紧的线，下端系着重物，垂得笔直。

abstract.en: Imagine looking down from high above at a tower that rises straight out of the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象从高空俯视一座从地面笔直竖起的塔。

abstract.en: Think of a page folded along its long side, so the fold runs from top to bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸沿长边对折，折痕从上一直通到底。

examples.en: The tower rises vertically above the harbour.
examples.cn: 高楼在港口上方垂直拔起。

examples.en: Please write the numbers vertically in this column.
examples.cn: 请在这一列里把数字竖着写。

examples.en: The two beams were not vertically aligned, so the frame leaned.
examples.cn: 两根横梁没有垂直对齐，所以框架歪了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「窝踢口里」——把东西竖着塞进窝里，要踢到口里；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vertere（转）→ vertex（转动的顶点、头顶）→ 拉丁 verticālis（头顶的、竖直的）→ 英语 vertical → vertically，核心义「沿上下笔直线」。

sensesIntro.en: Vertically starts from the plain up and down line, extends to a right angle with the ground and to any long axis, and then branches into layout, air travel, organisations, and writing.
sensesIntro.cn: vertically 从最朴素的上下直线出发，扩展到与地面成直角以及任何长轴，再分化为排版、空中运动、组织结构与书写等用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plumb line that hangs straight down to the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根笔直垂向地面的铅垂线。

branches.en: The plain up and down line is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 朴素的上下直线是日常义项。

branches.en: A right angle to the ground and a straight climb both follow the vertical line.
branches.cn: 与地面成直角以及径直上升，都沿着竖直线走。

branches.en: The long axis of a shape and a column of text share the same direction.
branches.cn: 形状的长轴与文字的列共用同一方向。

branches.en: A ladder from top to bottom turns into an organisational chain.
branches.cn: 从顶到底的梯子被引申为组织结构链条。

branches.en: Cutting through all layers and writing down the page both stretch the vertical idea.
branches.cn: 贯穿所有层级与沿页面向下书写，都延伸了竖直的观念。

intro.en: Vertically is a suffix-built adverb of the vertical family, with the Latin root vert and the adverb ending working together.
intro.cn: vertically 是由后缀构成的副词，属于 vertical 词族，拉丁词根 vert 与副词词尾共同作用。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere means to turn, and vertex means a whirl or the top of the head; the adverb ending adds the sense of manner.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 意为转动，vertex 意为旋涡或头顶；副词词尾则赋予它方式含义。

items.example: The root vert- appears in convert and reverse.
items.exampleCN: 词根 vert- 出现在 convert 与 reverse 中。

items.example: Vertere gives the turning idea behind vertex.
items.exampleCN: vertere 赋予 vertex 背后的转动意象。

items.meaning: a whirl, a peak, the top of the head
items.example: Vertex is the ancestor of vertical.
items.exampleCN: vertex 是 vertical 的祖先词。

items.example: The suffix -al forms vertical.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 vertical。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns vertical into vertically.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把 vertical 变成 vertically。

items.example: A vertical line runs up and down.
items.exampleCN: vertical 表示上下延伸的线。

items.meaning: in an up and down direction
items.example: Vertically describes how something is placed.
items.exampleCN: vertically 描述某物摆放的方式。

items.example: Verticality names the quality of standing upright.
items.exampleCN: verticality 指竖直的状态。

items.example: Invert shares the same turning root.
items.exampleCN: invert 共享同一个「转动」词根。

items.example: Divert also builds on the turning root.
items.exampleCN: divert 同样建立在「转动」词根上。

latinEntries.meaning: a whirl or the top of the head

definition_zh: 活力；热情；生机；才气；兴头
definition_en: great energy and enthusiasm, especially in the way someone performs, speaks, or creates
core_image: 乐手在舞台上挥动琴弓，眼睛里闪着光，整个人像被点着了
scene: 音乐节的最后一首曲子响起，主唱跳上音箱，扯开嗓子带着全场一起唱。The singer performed the last song with real verve.
sceneCN: 这里 verve 是「活力、热情」（第 1 个义项：做事时那种饱满的干劲与热情）；句意：歌手用十足的活力唱完了最后一首歌。

derivatives.zh: 同源词，本为拉丁语马鞭草，在现代英语中只作植物名，与「活力」义无关
罕见词，义为「马鞭草属的」，属同一植物词源，不是常用派生词

senses.title: Lively energy and enthusiasm
senses.definition: a lively energy that shows in the actions, speech, or manner of a person
senses.definitionCN: 从动作、言语或举止中透出的蓬勃精力
senses.example: She answered every question with verve.
senses.exampleCN: 她活力满满地一一回答了所有问题。
senses.why: The core image is a person in high spirits, so the first sense is simply that warm, lively drive made visible.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一个兴致高涨的人，所以第一个义项就是这种温暖而鲜活的冲劲直接显露出来。

senses.title: Spirit in performance or art
senses.definition: the particular liveliness that makes a performance, a piece of music, or a painting feel alive
senses.definitionCN: 让演出、乐曲或绘画显得有生命的独特生气
senses.example: The orchestra played the finale with unexpected verve.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队把终曲演奏得意外的神采飞扬。
senses.why: When the energy passes into a performance, sense 01 becomes the quality that makes the work feel animated rather than technically correct.
senses.whyCN: 当这种精力进入表演之中，第一个义项就变成让作品显得有生命而不只是技术正确的神采。

senses.title: Creative flair and wit
senses.definition: a sparkling cleverness or imaginative style, especially in writing or speech
senses.definitionCN: 尤指写作或言谈中闪光的机敏与想象力
senses.example: Her essay was praised for its wit and verve.
senses.exampleCN: 她的文章因机智与才气而受到称赞。
senses.why: Energy directed through words turns into flair, so the same word also names the bright, quick liveliness of style.
senses.whyCN: 精力经由文字表达出来就变成了才气，于是这个词也指文风上那种明快灵动。

senses.title: A rush of high spirits
senses.definition: a sudden burst of good spirits or bold impulse
senses.definitionCN: 突然涌起的好兴致或大胆冲动
senses.example: In a sudden fit of verve, he invited the whole street to dance.
senses.exampleCN: 他一时兴头上来，就邀请整条街的人跳舞。
senses.why: The lively state can be brief, so the noun also names a short surge of mood rather than a steady temperament.
senses.whyCN: 这种活跃状态可以很短暂，所以名词也能指一阵短暂上扬的心绪，而不是稳定的性情。

senses.title: Vigour in style or writing
senses.definition: forceful and energetic style, in writing or in visual design
senses.definitionCN: 写作或视觉设计中强劲有力的风格
senses.example: He paints with the same verve as he writes.
senses.exampleCN: 他作画的笔势与写作一样有力。
senses.why: Strong energy is felt as force, so verve also describes the driving power of a style rather than its cleverness.
senses.whyCN: 充沛的精力会被感受为力量，因此这个词也用来形容风格的推动力，而非机巧。

senses.title: Freshness of mind
senses.definition: a mental liveliness that keeps ideas fresh and quick
senses.definitionCN: 让想法新鲜、敏捷的头脑活跃状态
senses.example: Age had not dulled the verve of his thinking.
senses.exampleCN: 岁月并没有让他思维的清新变得迟钝。
senses.why: The energy picture can move from body to mind, describing an alertness that keeps ideas lively.
senses.whyCN: 这种精力图景可以从身体移到头脑，用来形容让想法保持鲜活的敏锐状态。

intro.en: Verve comes from French, where it first meant style or expression, and French took it from Latin verva, an old plural word for lively talk.
intro.cn: verve 来自法语，在法语中最初指风格或表达，而法语又承自拉丁语 verva，一个表示生动言辞的旧复数词。

items.en: Verva is a rare plural form used for words or expression, linked by some scholars to verba, words.
items.cn: verva 是少见的复数形式，指言辞或表达，部分学者把它与 verba（词语）联系起来。

items.en: Vervee appears in French for a lively or inventive turn of speech, though its exact path is uncertain.
items.cn: 法语中出现了 vervee，指生动而有创造力的说法，但其确切演变路径不确定。

items.en: Verve names the spirit of a writer, the spark that keeps a style lively.
items.cn: 法语 verve 指作家的灵气，即让文风保持鲜活的那点火花。

items.en: English borrows verve for energy of style, first in talk about literature and art.
items.cn: 英语借入 verve 表示文风上的劲道，起初多用于谈论文学与艺术。

items.en: Verve widens from style to spirits, describing lively manner, performance, and mood.
items.cn: 现代英语中 verve 从文风扩展到精神，形容有活力的举止、表演与心情。

note.en: Verve sits among words for liveliness and spirit, and looks close to verge, verse, and nerve only in spelling.
note.cn: verve 属于表示活力与精神的词群，与 verge、verse、nerve 只是拼写接近。

entries.definition: the edge or border of something
entries.definitionCN: 边缘；界限，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: writing arranged in lines with a rhythm
entries.definitionCN: 诗句；韵文，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: courage, or a fibre carrying signals in the body
entries.definitionCN: 勇气；神经，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: physical or mental strength and energy
liveliness, courage, or attitude
eager enjoyment and enthusiasm

normalIntro.en: Verve is the spark of a living performance: it enters English through French, and its short sound makes it easy to recall.
normalIntro.cn: verve 是生动表演里的火花：它经由法语进入英语，短促的读音也很容易记。

normal.en: With verve is a common phrase for doing something in a lively way.
normal.cn: 「with verve」是描述做事有活力的常见搭配。

normal.en: A performer full of verve makes a dull script feel exciting.
normal.cn: 一个充满 verve 的表演者能让乏味的剧本变得精彩。

normal.en: Verve is uncountable, so say with much verve, not with many verve.
normal.cn: verve 是不可数名词，应说许多活力，而不是多个活力。

normal.en: Reviewers often praise wit and verve together in a novel.
normal.cn: 书评常把小说的机智与才气放在一起称赞。

normal.en: Verve reached English from French, which gave it the sense of literary sparkle first.
normal.cn: verve 从法语进入英语，先带上文采闪光的含义。

abstract.en: Picture a drummer whose sticks blur, and the whole band speeds up.
abstract.cn: 想象鼓手的鼓槌快到模糊，整个乐队都跟着提速。

abstract.en: Imagine a dancer who still smiles during the hardest jump.
abstract.cn: 想象一位在最高难度跳跃时仍旧微笑的舞者。

abstract.en: Think of a pencil that moves so fast it seems to glow.
abstract.cn: 想象一支铅笔写得飞快，仿佛在发亮。

examples.en: The team tackled the problem with verve.
examples.cn: 团队满怀干劲地着手解决这个问题。

examples.en: His letters are full of verve and humour.
examples.cn: 他的书信才气横溢又幽默。

examples.en: The young band plays with a verve that older acts often lose.
examples.cn: 这支年轻乐队演奏时的活力，是老乐队往往已经失去的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吻我」——舞台上歌手激情四射，观众喊吻我；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 verva（生动的言辞，来源一般认为与 verba「词语」有关，但存疑）→ 法语 verve（文采、灵气）→ 英语 verve，核心义「一股鲜活的生命力」。

sensesIntro.en: Verve begins as a lively drive, passes through performance and creative flair, and spreads out into mood, style, and the freshness of the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: verve 起于一股鲜活的冲劲，流经表演与才气，再扩散到情绪、文风与头脑的清新。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a performer whose whole body shines with energy.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个全身闪着活力的表演者。

branches.en: Visible energy in a person is the base sense.
branches.cn: 人身上看得见的精力是基础义项。

branches.en: Energy passed into a work becomes spirit and vigour of style.
branches.cn: 精力进入作品后，就成为作品的神采与气势。

branches.en: Energy through words becomes wit and flair.
branches.cn: 精力经由文字就变成机敏与才气。

branches.en: A short burst of good spirits is the mood sense.
branches.cn: 短暂涌起的好兴致是情绪义项。

branches.en: The same liveliness moved inward describes a fresh mind.
branches.cn: 同样的活跃转向内部，就描述清新的头脑。

intro.en: Verve has no transparent English affixes; instead it is a loanword that brought its French family along.
intro.cn: verve 没有可以拆解的英语词缀，它是一个带着法语词族一起进入英语的借词。

latinIntro.en: Latin verva, a lively form of speech, is the likely distant source, with French verve as the direct donor word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 verva（生动的言辞）是较远的可能来源，法语 verve 则是直接借入词。

items.example: Verve is uncountable in standard English.
items.exampleCN: verve 在标准英语中是不可数名词。

items.meaning: a rare form for words or expression
items.meaningCN: 指言辞或表达的少见词形
items.example: Verva is a rare plural noun in Latin.
items.exampleCN: verva 是拉丁语中少见的复数名词。

items.example: Vervee is the likely French forerunner.
items.exampleCN: vervee 很可能是法语中的前身词。

items.example: French verve names a writer spirit.
items.exampleCN: 法语 verve 指作家的灵气。

items.example: Verb shares the distant Latin words for speech.
items.exampleCN: verb 与表示言辞的拉丁词有遥远的关联。

items.example: Verbal also comes from the Latin word for word.
items.exampleCN: verbal 同样来自拉丁语的「词」一词。

items.example: Proverb is built from the same speaking root.
items.exampleCN: proverb 建立在同一个「言说」词根上。

items.example: Verbiage keeps the idea of words without liveliness.
items.exampleCN: verbiage 保留了「言辞」的想法，却没有了活力。

items.example: Reverb is a modern echo of the same ver- shape, from a different root.
items.exampleCN: reverb 只是外形相近的现代词，词根并不相同。

definition_zh: 背心；马甲；防护衣；授予；赋予
definition_en: a sleeveless garment worn on the upper body, or to give a power or right to someone in a formal way
core_image: 一件贴身套在衬衫外面的短背心，前后各开一道扣
scene: 早上出门买咖啡，店员穿着一件深蓝色针织背心，正利落地给客人的杯子盖盖子。He wore a navy vest under his jacket.
sceneCN: 这里 vest 是「背心、马甲」（第 1 个义项：无袖、套在上身的衣物）；句意：他在外套里面穿了一件藏青色背心。

collocations.phrase: the estate vests in the heir

derivatives.zh: 由动词加过去分词构成形容词，义为「法律上已归属的；既得的」
由动词加 -ing 构成名词，义为「权益授予；归属生效」
加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「法衣；祭服」
加名词后缀构成，义为「教堂更衣室；教区委员会」

senses.title: A short sleeveless piece of clothing
senses.definition: a short garment with no sleeves, worn on the upper body over a shirt or under a jacket
senses.definitionCN: 一种无袖的短衣物，套在衬衫外或穿在外套里，覆盖上身
senses.example: He pulled on a wool vest before stepping outside.
senses.exampleCN: 他出门前套上了一件羊毛背心。
senses.why: The core image is a simple covering slipped over the head, and clothing remains the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象就是从头套下的一件简单衣物，所以衣物仍是日常义项。

senses.title: Protective gear worn on the torso
senses.definition: a garment worn for protection, such as a life vest or a bullet-proof vest
senses.definitionCN: 为保护身体而穿的衣物，如救生衣、防弹背心
senses.example: Every passenger must wear a life vest during the drill.
senses.exampleCN: 演练期间每位乘客都必须穿上救生衣。
senses.why: The sleeveless shape becomes a shell around the body, so it is borrowed for protective gear that fits over clothing.
senses.whyCN: 无袖的形制变成包裹身体的一层壳，于是被借用来指套在衣服外的防护装备。

senses.title: A sleeveless top for sport
senses.definition: a light sleeveless shirt, especially one worn by runners or players
senses.definitionCN: 轻便的无袖上衣，尤指跑步或比赛时穿的背心
senses.example: The runners wore numbered vests in the race.
senses.exampleCN: 跑者们在比赛中穿着带号码的背心。
senses.why: Sport turns the old under-layer into a visible outer shirt, keeping the same sleeveless shape.
senses.whyCN: 运动场景把旧时的内衬衣物变成显眼的外穿背心，但保留无袖的形制。

senses.title: To give a right or power formally
senses.definition: to give power, authority, or a legal right to a person or body in a formal way
senses.definitionCN: 正式把权力、职权或法定权利授予某人或某机构
senses.example: The constitution vests the power of lawmaking in the parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 宪法把立法权授予议会。
senses.why: In law the word passed from putting on a garment to putting authority on a person, as if rights were clothing handed over.
senses.whyCN: 在法律语境中，这个词从穿上衣服引申为把权力「穿」到某人身上，仿佛把权利当作衣物交付过去。

senses.title: For a right to become settled in someone
senses.definition: of a right, power, or benefit, to pass to someone and remain legally fixed in them
senses.definitionCN: 指权利、权力或利益归属于某人并在法律上固定下来
senses.example: The pension vests after ten years of service.
senses.exampleCN: 养老金在服务满十年后归属生效。
senses.why: Once an authority is on a person, it stays, so the verb also describes how a right finally belongs to its holder.
senses.whyCN: 一旦权力到了某人身上就会留下，于是这个动词也描述某项权利最终归属于持有人的过程。

senses.title: To dress someone in ceremonial robes
senses.definition: to dress a person, especially a priest or ruler, in ceremonial clothes
senses.definitionCN: 给某人，尤指祭司或君主，穿上礼服
senses.example: The bishop was vested in white before the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式开始前，主教换上了白色法衣。
senses.why: The ordinary clothing sense survives in formal dress, where someone is vested with robes of office.
senses.whyCN: 普通衣物之义在礼服中保留下来，于是有了「为某人穿上身上的礼服」这一用法。

senses.title: The American word for a waistcoat
senses.definition: in American English, the three-piece suit garment worn over a shirt and under a jacket
senses.definitionCN: 在美式英语中，指三件套西装里套在衬衫外、外套内的一件
senses.example: His wedding suit came with a matching vest.
senses.exampleCN: 他的婚礼西装配有一件同款马甲。
senses.why: Since British and American speakers split the old words, one garment is called a vest on one side of the Atlantic and a waistcoat on the other.
senses.whyCN: 英美两地分割了旧词，同一种衣物在大西洋两岸分别叫 vest 和 waistcoat。

senses.title: A sleeveless garment for covering the body
senses.definition: an old or literary word for a garment worn on the upper body
senses.definitionCN: 上身躯干的旧称或书面说法
senses.example: The knight tore his silken vest in the fight.
senses.exampleCN: 骑士在打斗中撕破了他的丝质上衣。
senses.why: The Latin ancestor meant any garment, so vest has an older general sense that survives only in literature and history.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语祖先泛指任何衣裳，所以 vest 保留了一个更泛的旧义，如今只见于文学与历史书写。

intro.en: Vest comes through French from Latin vestis, a garment, and vestire, to clothe, which also gave invest and divest.
intro.cn: vest 经法语来自拉丁语 vestis（衣裳）与 vestire（穿衣），同样源头也生出 invest 与 divest。

items.en: A reconstructed root for clothing, often written wes, lies behind the word, though the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词背后有一个表示「穿衣」的原始印欧语词根，通常写作 wes，但确切形式存疑。

items.en: Vestis means a garment and vestire means to clothe.
items.cn: vestis 意为衣裳，vestire 意为给……穿衣。

items.en: Veste or vestir carries the clothing word into French and on to English.
items.cn: veste 或 vestir 把衣物词带入法语，再进入英语。

items.en: Vest enters English as a robe or outer garment, and the verb means to clothe.
items.cn: vest 作为袍服或外衣进入英语，动词义为给……穿衣。

items.en: In law, to vest a right means to put it in someone, and the right is said to vest in them.
items.cn: 法律中 vest a right 指把权利授予某人，权利则被说成 vest in 某人。

items.en: The noun narrows to the sleeveless garment, with American vest used for the British waistcoat.
items.cn: 名词义收窄为无袖背心，美式的 vest 对应英式的 waistcoat。

note.en: Vest is the clothing noun of the vestis family and also a legal verb, close to invest, divest, and the garment words nearby.
note.cn: vest 既是 vestis 词族里的衣物名词，又是法律动词，与 invest、divest 以及邻近的衣物词相关。

entries.definition: to put money in, or to give a power or quality
to take something away from someone
legally fixed to a person
a sleeveless garment worn under a jacket
a light shirt worn under other clothes
a shirt with no sleeves and narrow straps

normalIntro.en: Vest is the garment word that also dresses a right in law: put it on as clothes, give it out as authority.
normalIntro.cn: vest 既是衣物词，也能给法律上的权利「穿衣」：当作衣服穿上，也当作权力授予。

normal.en: A vest has no sleeves, so it fits close to the body.
normal.cn: 背心没有袖子，所以贴身合体。

normal.en: Remember the family: invest puts money or power in, divest takes it out.
normal.cn: 记住词族：invest 把金钱或权力投入，divest 把它撤走。

normal.en: In law a power vests in a body, meaning it is given to that body and stays there.
normal.cn: 法律中某项权力 vest in 某机构，意即授予该机构并留存在那里。

normal.en: British speakers say waistcoat for the suit garment that American speakers call a vest.
normal.cn: 英式说 waistcoat，美式说 vest，指的是西装里的那件马甲。

normal.en: A bullet-proof vest and a life vest use the word for protection.
normal.cn: 防弹背心与救生衣都用这个词表示防护。

abstract.en: Picture a runner pulling on a number vest just before the start.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者在起跑前套上带号码的背心。

abstract.en: Imagine a lawyer draping a signed right like a coat over a client.
abstract.cn: 想象律师把一份签署好的权利像大衣一样披在委托人身上。

abstract.en: Think of a coastguard handing out bright life vests on a boat.
abstract.cn: 想象海岸警卫队在船上发放鲜艳的救生衣。

examples.en: The children wore vests over their shirts in the cold.
examples.cn: 天冷时孩子们在衬衫外面穿着背心。

examples.en: The company vests full ownership of the shares after three years.
examples.cn: 三年后，公司把股份的完整所有权授予员工。

examples.en: He put on a life vest before the boat left the shore.
examples.cn: 小船离岸前他穿上了救生衣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外斯特」——外面套一件，最斯文的就是背心；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vestis（衣裳）+ vestire（穿衣）→ 古法语 → 中古英语 vest（袍服）→ 现代英语 vest（背心）与法律动词 vest（授予、归属）；同源还有 invest、divest。

sensesIntro.en: Vest begins as any garment, narrows to the sleeveless piece of clothing, and at the same time turns in law into giving or fixing a right in someone.
sensesIntro.cn: vest 最初泛指衣裳，后来收窄为无袖的背心，同时又在法律语境中转义为把权利授予或归属于某人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plain garment pulled on over the head.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件从头套下的朴素衣物。

branches.en: The garment sense runs from the old general word to the modern short vest.
branches.cn: 衣物义从旧的泛指一路延伸到现代短背心。

branches.en: A close covering becomes protective gear and a sports top.
branches.cn: 贴身覆盖物化身防护装备与运动背心。

branches.en: Giving out authority and fixing it in a holder are the legal pair.
branches.cn: 授出权力与把权力固定在持有人身上，构成法律上的一对。

branches.en: Dressing in robes keeps the oldest clothing action.
branches.cn: 给某人穿礼服保留了最古老的穿衣动作。

branches.en: American usage names the suit waistcoat a vest.
branches.cn: 美式用法把西装马甲称为 vest。

intro.en: Vest is not built from affixes but is the base of a Latin clothing family, with in-, di-, and -ed modifying it.
intro.cn: vest 并非由词缀组合而成，而是一个拉丁「衣物」词族的基础词，in-、di- 与 -ed 分别在其上添加修饰。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestis means garment and vestire means to clothe; the English family keeps both the clothing and the giving-away senses.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestis 意为衣裳，vestire 意为穿衣；英语词族同时保留衣物义与移转义。

items.example: Vestis is the source of vest.
items.exampleCN: vestis 是 vest 的来源。

items.example: Vestire gives the verb to clothe a person.
items.exampleCN: vestire 提供「给某人穿衣」的动词义。

items.example: Vest narrows to the short sleeveless top.
items.exampleCN: vest 收窄为无袖短背心。

items.meaning: to give a right to someone
items.example: Vest as a verb belongs to law.
items.exampleCN: 作动词的 vest 属于法律用语。

items.example: The prefix in- forms invest.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成 invest。

items.meaning: to put in money or power
items.example: Invest literally means to put a garment on.
items.exampleCN: invest 字面上是「把衣裳穿上」。

items.example: The prefix di- forms divest.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 di- 构成 divest。

items.meaning: to take away or strip off
items.example: Divest means to strip a garment off.
items.exampleCN: divest 意为把衣裳剥下来。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms vested.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 vested。

items.example: Vested rights are rights already held.
items.exampleCN: vested rights 指已经持有的权利。

definition_zh: 遗迹；痕迹；残余；（某品质的）一丝；退化器官
definition_en: a trace or small remaining part of something that has almost disappeared
core_image: 沙滩上几乎被潮水抹平的脚印，只剩一道浅痕
scene: 潮水退去，沙滩上只剩一串被抹得几乎看不清的脚印。By morning only a few faint vestiges of the footprints were left on the sand.
sceneCN: 这里 vestige 是「痕迹、残迹」（第 2 个义项：留下的微弱痕迹）；句意：到早晨，沙滩上只剩几个淡淡的脚印痕迹。

pos.zh: 遗迹；痕迹；残余；一丝；退化器官

collocations.zh: 最后的残余；仅剩的残迹
一丝；一点儿（多用于否定）
消失得无影无踪；不留一丝遗迹

derivatives.zh: 遗迹的；退化的（多用于 vestigial organ 等结构）
拉丁语原形，意为「脚印、痕迹」，是英语词的直接来源
