senses.title: A footprint or trace left on the ground
senses.definition: a mark left by a foot, a wheel, or a moving thing on the ground
senses.definitionCN: 脚、车轮或移动物体在地面上留下的印记
senses.example: The hunters followed the vestiges of a deer in the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 猎人们循着泥地里鹿的足迹跟了过去。
senses.why: Latin vestigium first meant the print of a foot, so the word begins as a visible mark on the ground.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vestigium 最初指脚的印痕，所以这个词的起点是留在地面上的可见印记。

senses.title: A faint trace of something that has gone
senses.definition: a small sign that something used to exist but has largely disappeared
senses.definitionCN: 表明某事物曾经存在、如今已大部分消失的微弱迹象
senses.example: Only a few vestiges of the old wall remain.
senses.exampleCN: 旧城墙只剩下几处残迹。
senses.why: From the literal footprint, the sense widens to any faint trace left behind by a thing that has passed.
senses.whyCN: 从字面上的脚印，词义扩展到任何事物经过后留下的微弱痕迹。

senses.title: A small surviving remainder
senses.definition: a very small part of something that continues to exist after most of it is gone
senses.definitionCN: 某事物大部分消失后仍然存续的极小部分
senses.example: The last vestiges of the empire vanished in the war.
senses.exampleCN: 帝国的最后残余在战火中消失了。
senses.why: Once a trace is standing for a whole that has almost gone, it can also name that leftover part itself.
senses.whyCN: 当痕迹代表几乎消失的整体时，它也可以指代那一点留下来的部分本身。

senses.title: The smallest amount of a quality
senses.titleCN: 一丝；一点儿（常用于否定）
senses.definition: a tiny amount of a feeling or quality, especially when none at all is expected
senses.definitionCN: 某种情感或品质的极小分量，尤指本不该有的情况
senses.example: There was not a vestige of doubt in her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的声音里没有一丝疑问。
senses.why: If a vestige is the least visible mark of a thing, in negations it becomes the least possible amount of it.
senses.whyCN: 既然 vestige 是一事物最微弱的印迹，那么在否定句里它就成了该事物可能存在的最小量。

senses.title: A remnant organ left by evolution
senses.definition: a body part that has lost most of its function through evolution but is still present
senses.definitionCN: 在进化过程中已丧失大部分功能、却仍然存在的身体结构
senses.example: Biologists regard the appendix as a vestige of an earlier digestive organ.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家把阑尾看作早期消化器官的残存结构。
senses.why: Biology borrows the trace sense for parts that survive only as leftovers of an earlier form.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了「痕迹」这一义项，指仅作为早期形态遗留物而存下来的结构。

intro.en: Vestige comes from Latin vestigium, a footprint or trace, through French.
intro.cn: vestige 经由法语来自拉丁语 vestigium（脚印、痕迹）。

items.en: Vestigium means a footprint, a track, or a trace.
items.cn: vestigium 意为脚印、足迹或痕迹。

items.en: Vestigare, to track or follow a trail, is formed from the same stem.
items.cn: vestigare 意为循迹追踪，由同一词干构成。

items.en: Vestige is recorded in French, still naming a footprint or a mark.
items.cn: 法语中已有 vestige，仍指脚印或印记。

items.en: English adopts the word in the sense of a trace or a mark left behind.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪引入该词，意为残留下来的痕迹或印记。

items.en: The word spreads to remainders of empires, civilizations, and body organs.
items.cn: 现代英语中，词义扩展到帝国、文明的残迹以及身体的退化器官。

note.en: Vestige is the trace left on the ground, close to vestigial and to ordinary words for remains.
note.cn: vestige 是留在地面上的痕迹，与 vestigial 以及表示「残余」的普通词相邻。

entries.definition: remaining as a small trace, often of an organ that has lost its use
an entrance hall or a small space at the end of a canal
entries.definitionCN: 门厅；前室（只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自拉丁语 vestibulum）

entries.definition: to follow a trail of evidence in order to find the truth
entries.definitionCN: 调查；追查（与 vestigare「循迹追踪」同源）

entries.definition: a very small sign that something existed
a small part that is left after the rest has gone
an object or custom surviving from an earlier time

normalIntro.en: Vestige is Latin vestigium, a footprint: the mark still visible after the traveller has gone.
normalIntro.cn: vestige 源于拉丁语 vestigium，即脚印：旅人走后仍能看见的那道印。

normal.en: The plural is vestiges, used mostly in formal descriptions of traces.
normal.cn: 复数是 vestiges，多用于正式地描述残迹。

normal.en: The last vestiges of the old palace are now under the sand.
normal.cn: the last vestiges of 表示「最后的残迹」，旧宫殿只剩沙下的残迹。

normal.en: Without a vestige of doubt means with complete certainty.
normal.cn: without a vestige of doubt 意为毫无一丝怀疑。

normal.en: The adjective vestigial appears in vestigial organ and vestigial wings.
normal.cn: 形容词 vestigial 见于 vestigial organ（退化器官）与 vestigial wings（退化翅膀）。

normal.en: Investigate shares the tracking stem, since the Romans tracked the vestigia of a trail.
normal.cn: investigate 与它共享「追踪」词干，因为古罗马人循着足迹追踪线索。

abstract.en: Picture a wet footprint drying slowly on stone until only a shadow of it is left.
abstract.cn: 想象石板上一个湿脚印慢慢变干，最后只剩一层淡淡的影子。

abstract.en: Think of a museum room where ruins are shown by a faint outline on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象博物馆用地面上的淡淡轮廓来标示一片遗址的位置。

abstract.en: See an empire shrinking to a single old coin kept in a glass case.
abstract.cn: 想象一个帝国缩小成玻璃柜里的一枚旧钱币。

examples.en: The last vestiges of the ancient city lie beneath the fields.
examples.cn: 这座古城的最后遗迹埋在田野之下。

examples.en: She showed not a vestige of fear when the lights went out.
examples.cn: 灯灭的时候，她没有流露一丝恐惧。

examples.en: Some snakes keep vestiges of hind limbs as tiny bones.
examples.cn: 有些蛇只把后肢的残迹留作极小的骨头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「微丝迹」——只剩一「微」小的一「丝」痕「迹」，正好指 vestige 的残迹义；这只是谐音拆解，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vestigium（脚印、痕迹）→ 古法语 vestige → 英语 vestige，同源动词 vestigare 意为「循迹追踪」，核心义「留下的微小印迹」。

sensesIntro.en: Vestige starts as a footprint, widens to any faint trace, then to the small part left over, a tiny amount, and finally a body part left by evolution.
sensesIntro.cn: vestige 从脚印起步，扩展到任何微弱的痕迹，再指留下来的那一点部分、极小的分量，最后指进化留下的退化器官。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a footprint fading on the sand.
core.cn: 核心意象：正在沙地上淡去的脚印。

branches.en: A footprint is the oldest and most concrete sense.
branches.cn: 脚印是最古老、最具体的义项。

branches.en: Any faint trace of a lost thing grows from the footprint.
branches.cn: 任何失去事物的微弱痕迹，都由脚印义生长而来。

branches.en: The leftover part itself is the following step.
branches.cn: 留下来的那部分本身是紧接的一步。

branches.en: A tiny quantity is the most abstract use of the same idea.
branches.cn: 极小的分量是同一理念最抽象的用法。

branches.en: The biological remnant applies the trace image to anatomy.
branches.cn: 生物学上的残存结构把痕迹意象用于解剖学。

intro.en: Vestige is a borrowed Latin noun, with English vestigial and the same-root verb investigate built around it.
intro.cn: vestige 是借用的拉丁语名词，英语围绕它构成 vestigial，并有同根动词 investigate。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestigium means a footprint, and vestigare means to track.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestigium 意为脚印，vestigare 意为追踪。

items.example: Vestigium is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: vestigium 是英语词的直接来源。

items.meaning: to track, to follow a trail
items.example: Vestigare gives the idea of following a trail.
items.exampleCN: vestigare 给出循迹追踪的意象。

items.meaning: to search into, to track down
items.example: Investigare is the parent of English investigate.
items.exampleCN: investigare 是英语 investigate 的前身。

items.example: The suffix -ial turns vestige into vestigial.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ial 把 vestige 变成 vestigial。

items.example: Vestigial organs were once useful body parts.
items.exampleCN: vestigial 器官曾是身体有用的部分。

items.meaning: to follow evidence and find out
items.example: Investigate keeps the tracking image of the root.
items.exampleCN: investigate 保留了词根的追踪意象。

items.example: Investigation is the noun built on investigate.
items.exampleCN: investigation 是在 investigate 基础上构成的名词。

items.meaning: a person who looks into a case
items.example: An investigator follows the tracks of evidence.
items.exampleCN: 调查员沿着证据的踪迹追查。

items.example: The phrase sums up the leftover sense of vestige.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语概括了 vestige 的残余义。

definition_zh: 兽医；兽医职业者
definition_en: a doctor whose work is to treat sick and injured animals
core_image: 一位女医生在农场的谷仓里给一头奶牛检查腿伤
scene: 谷仓里的奶牛瘸着腿，主人慌忙请来一位穿工作服的医生给它检查。The worried farmer called a veterinarian to examine the limping cow.
sceneCN: 这里 veterinarian 是「兽医」（第 1 个义项：给动物治病的医生）；句意：焦急的农场主请来一位兽医给那头瘸腿的奶牛检查。

collocations.phrase: take the dog to the veterinarian

derivatives.zh: 兽医的；与动物医疗有关的（名词去后缀 -ian 即为形容词）
兽医（veterinarian 在英国口语中的缩略形式）
兽医工作；兽医职业（较少见的名词化形式）

senses.title: A doctor who treats animals
senses.definition: a person trained in the medical care of animals and licensed to treat them
senses.definitionCN: 接受过动物医疗训练并获得执业资格、给动物治病的人
senses.example: The veterinarian gave the puppy its first shots.
senses.exampleCN: 兽医给小狗打了第一针疫苗。
senses.why: Latin veterina meant beasts of burden, and a veterinarius looked after them, so the word names the livestock doctor from the start.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 veterina 指驮畜，veterinarius 指照料驮畜的人，所以这个词从一开始就指牲畜医生。

senses.title: The animal-care profession
senses.definition: the profession or practice of caring for the health of animals
senses.definitionCN: 照料动物健康的职业或从业活动
senses.example: She has worked in veterinarian practice for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在兽医行业工作了二十年。
senses.why: A title for one person can also stand for the whole occupation, which is how profession words usually widen.
senses.whyCN: 指代一个人的头衔也可以代表整个职业，这是职业名词常见的扩展方式。

senses.title: A trained specialist for a species
senses.definition: a veterinarian who specialises in one kind of animal or one branch of animal medicine
senses.definitionCN: 专攻某一类动物或某一动物医学分支的兽医
senses.example: The zoo hired a veterinarian specialising in large animals.
senses.exampleCN: 动物园聘请了一位专攻大型动物的兽医。
senses.why: As animal medicine grew into specialities, the general title split into named branches such as large-animal work.
senses.whyCN: 随着动物医学发展出专科，这个通称也分出了大型动物等具体的分支名称。

intro.en: Veterinarian comes from Latin veterinarius, a worker who looked after beasts of burden, with the noun ending -ian added in English.
intro.cn: veterinarian 来自拉丁语 veterinarius（照料驮畜的人），英语再加名词后缀 -ian 构成。

items.en: Veterina means beasts of burden, the pack horses and oxen of a farm.
items.cn: veterina 指驮畜，即农场的驮马与牛。

items.en: Veterinarius describes whatever belongs to such beasts, and names the man who cares for them.
items.cn: veterinarius 描述与这类牲畜有关的事物，也指照料它们的人。

items.en: The word root is uncertain; it is often linked to vetus, old, and compared with veteranus, an old soldier.
items.cn: 该词的词根来源不确定，一般认为与 vetus（年老的）相关，并可与 veteranus（老兵）对照，此说仅为推测。

items.en: English borrows veterinary in the sense of relating to the medical treatment of animals.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 veterinary，意为与动物医疗有关的。

items.en: Veterinarian appears as the noun for the animal doctor, and veterinary surgeon appears beside it.
items.cn: 十八至十九世纪，veterinarian 作为「兽医」的名词出现，veterinary surgeon 的说法也随之出现。

items.en: American usage prefers veterinarian, while British speech shortens it to vet.
items.cn: 现代英语中，美国用法常用 veterinarian，而英国口语把它缩略为 vet。

note.en: Veterinarian is the person, veterinary is the adjective, and vet is the everyday short form.
note.cn: veterinarian 指人，veterinary 是形容词，vet 是日常缩略形式。

entries.definition: relating to the medical care of animals
the everyday short word for an animal doctor
a person who has long experience, especially an old soldier
entries.definitionCN: 老兵；老手（只是拼写相近，来自拉丁语 vetus「年老的」，词源与兽医不同）

entries.definition: a doctor who performs operations on people
entries.definitionCN: 外科医生（对象通常是人）

entries.definition: a doctor of medicine who treats people without surgery
a scientist who studies animals as living things
entries.definitionCN: 动物学家（研究动物本身，而非治病）

normalIntro.en: Veterinarian is veterinary plus -ian: the person who practises veterinary medicine.
normalIntro.cn: veterinarian 是 veterinary 加 -ian：从事兽医医疗这一行业的人。

normal.en: Veterinary is the adjective, and -ian names the person, as with mathematics and mathematician.
normal.cn: veterinary 是形容词，词尾 -ian 表示人，正如 mathematics 与 mathematician 的关系。

normal.en: Farms once needed a veterinarius for their oxen and horses, hence the animal link.
normal.cn: 农场曾需要 veterinarius 照料牛马，因此这个词与动物紧密相连。

normal.en: Take the dog to the veterinarian is the most common sentence pattern.
normal.cn: 「take the dog to the veterinarian」是最常见的句型，意思是带狗去看兽医。

normal.en: British speech says vet, and American speech keeps the long veterinarian.
normal.cn: 英国口语说 vet，美国口语保留完整的 veterinarian。

normal.en: A veterinarian is not a physician, since a physician treats people.
normal.cn: veterinarian 不是 physician，因为 physician 给人看病。

abstract.en: Picture a barn door opening and a doctor arriving with a leather bag of animal medicine.
abstract.cn: 想象谷仓门打开，一位医生提着装满兽药的皮包走进来。

abstract.en: See a farmer holding a restless lamb while the doctor listens to its heart.
abstract.cn: 想象农民抱着一只不安的小羊，医生在听它的心跳。

abstract.en: Think of a row of waiting pets outside a clinic, each with an anxious owner.
abstract.cn: 想象诊所门外排着等候的宠物，每只旁边都有一位着急的主人。

examples.en: The veterinarian warned that the horse needed rest for a month.
examples.cn: 兽医提醒说这匹马需要休息一个月。

examples.en: As a veterinarian, she now works mostly with dairy cattle.
examples.cn: 作为兽医，她现在主要诊治奶牛。

examples.en: Our veterinarian suggested changing the cat to a different diet.
examples.cn: 我们的兽医建议给猫换一种饮食。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂特 veterinarian」——专门「喂」养「特」别需要照顾的动物的人，就是兽医；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 veterina（驮畜）+ -arius（从事……的人）→ veterinarius（照料驮畜的人）→ 英语 veterinary（形容词）与 veterinarian（名词），核心义「照料牲畜的人」。词根可能与 vetus（年老的）相关，但来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Veterinarian names one animal doctor, then the whole profession, and finally the specialist within it.
sensesIntro.cn: veterinarian 先指一位给动物治病的医生，再指整个兽医行业，最后指其中某一领域的专科兽医。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doctor walking into a barn to check a sick cow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位兽医走进谷仓为病牛检查。

branches.en: The single practitioner is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 单个从业者是基本义项。

branches.en: The profession sense extends the person to the occupation.
branches.cn: 职业义项把指人的词扩展到整个行业。

branches.en: The specialist sense narrows the person to one branch.
branches.cn: 专科义项把指人的词收窄到某一分支。

branches.en: One veterinarian stands for a career that many people now follow.
branches.cn: 一位兽医代表了许多人如今从事的职业。

branches.en: The general doctor and the specialist share the same licence and years of training.
branches.cn: 普通兽医与专科兽医共享同样的执照与多年训练。

intro.en: Veterinarian is built on veterinary plus -ian, beside vet and the Latin source veterinarius.
intro.cn: veterinarian 由 veterinary 加 -ian 构成，旁边还有缩略词 vet 与拉丁来源 veterinarius。

latinIntro.en: Latin veterina means beasts of burden, and veterinarius means belonging to them or the man who tends them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 veterina 意为驮畜，veterinarius 意为与驮畜有关的或照料驮畜的人。

items.example: Veterina names the oxen and horses of a farm.
items.exampleCN: veterina 指农场的牛马等驮畜。

items.meaning: of beasts of burden, and the man who tends them
items.example: Veterinarius is the direct ancestor of the English word.
items.exampleCN: veterinarius 是英语词的直接祖先。

items.example: The suffix -ary gives the adjective veterinary.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 构成形容词 veterinary。

items.meaning: relating to the medical care of animals
items.example: Veterinary describes clinics, medicine, and surgery for animals.
items.exampleCN: veterinary 描述面向动物的诊所、药品与外科。

items.meaning: a person who practises or deals with
items.example: The suffix -ian turns veterinary into veterinarian.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ian 把 veterinary 变成 veterinarian。

items.example: The animal doctor is called a veterinarian.
items.exampleCN: 给动物看病的医生称为 veterinarian。

items.meaning: the short everyday word for the animal doctor
items.example: Vet clips the long word in British speech.
items.exampleCN: 英国口语把长词缩略为 vet。

items.meaning: the older full title of the animal doctor
items.example: Veterinary surgeon was the formal title clipped to vet.
items.exampleCN: veterinary surgeon 是被缩略为 vet 的正式头衔。

items.meaning: a person who helps the animal doctor
items.example: The veterinarian assistant held the dog still.
items.exampleCN: 兽医助理把狗按住不动。

definition_zh: 兽医的；兽医学的；动物医疗的
definition_en: relating to the medical care and treatment of animals
core_image: 诊室墙上挂着动物解剖图，台上有听诊器和奶牛的蹄铁
scene: 学生翻看兽医药物的说明书，书页上画着狗、牛和马的剪影。The label lists the veterinary uses of the medicine for dogs, cattle and horses.
sceneCN: 这里 veterinary 是「兽医的、动物医疗的」（第 1 个义项：与动物医疗有关的形容词）；句意：标签上列出了这种药物在狗、牛和马身上的兽医用途。

pos.zh: 兽医的；兽医学的；动物医疗的
兽医（多见于英式说法，为 veterinary surgeon 的缩略）

derivatives.zh: 兽医（veterinary 加 -ian 构成，多用于美式）
兽医（veterinary surgeon 的口语缩略）；v. 检查；审查
拉丁语原形，指照料驮畜的人，是英语词的直接来源

senses.title: Relating to the treatment of animals
senses.definition: connected with the medical care of animals
senses.definitionCN: 与动物的医疗照料有关的
senses.example: The clinic offers veterinary care for farm animals.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所提供农场动物的兽医护理。
senses.why: Latin veterinarius meant of beasts of burden, so the adjective has pointed to animal care since its origin.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 veterinarius 意为驮畜的，所以这个形容词从起源起就指向动物的照料。

senses.title: The branch of medical science for animals
senses.definition: the science and study of animal health and disease
senses.definitionCN: 研究动物健康与疾病的科学
senses.example: She studied veterinary science before opening her own clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 她学习兽医学之后开了自己的诊所。
senses.why: When an adjective is fixed to a noun such as science or medicine, it can name the field itself.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词与 science、medicine 等名词固定搭配时，它就可以指称整个学科领域。

senses.title: The animal doctor in British speech
senses.definition: the short British noun for a veterinary surgeon
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中 veterinary surgeon 的缩略名词
senses.example: The veterinary looked at the injured sheep at once.
senses.exampleCN: 兽医马上查看了受伤的羊。
senses.why: British usage clips the title veterinary surgeon to veterinary, so the adjective also works as a noun for the person.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语把 veterinary surgeon 这一头衔缩略为 veterinary，于是这个形容词也兼作指人的名词。

intro.en: Veterinary comes from Latin veterinarius, of beasts of burden, from veterina, the pack animals themselves.
intro.cn: veterinary 来自拉丁语 veterinarius（驮畜的），源于 veterina（驮畜本身）。

items.en: Veterina means beasts of burden, the oxen and horses kept for heavy work.
items.cn: veterina 指驮畜，即用来干重活的牛马。

items.en: Veterinarius forms an adjective meaning of such beasts, and also names their keeper.
items.cn: veterinarius 构成意为「此类牲畜的」的形容词，也指照料它们的人。

items.en: The deeper root is uncertain; it is commonly compared with vetus, old, and with veteranus, an old soldier, but this link is not proved.
items.cn: 更深的词根来源不确定，常被与 vetus（年老的）和 veteranus（老兵）相比较，但这一联系并未得到证实。

items.en: English borrows veterinary as an adjective for matters of animal medicine.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 veterinary，作形容词指与动物医疗相关的事物。

items.en: Veterinary engineering and veterinary surgery spread the word into professional titles.
items.cn: 兽医学教育与兽医外科把这一词带入了各种专业头衔。

items.en: The adjective now fixes to medicine, school, and clinic, and also serves as a British noun.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个形容词常与 medicine、school、clinic 搭配，并兼作英式名词。

note.en: Veterinary is the adjective behind veterinarian and vet, and sits beside words for animal studies.
note.cn: veterinary 是 veterinarian 与 vet 背后的形容词，旁边还有表示动物研究的词。

entries.definition: a doctor who treats animals
the clipped word for the animal doctor
an experienced person, especially an old soldier
entries.definitionCN: 老兵；老手（只是拼写相近，来自 vetus「年老的」，词源与兽医不同）

entries.definition: relating to medicine and the treatment of people
entries.definitionCN: 医学的；医疗的（对象通常是人）

entries.definition: relating to operations carried out by a surgeon
relating to the scientific study of animals
entries.definitionCN: 动物学的（研究动物本身，而非治病）

normalIntro.en: Veterinary is the adjective: it always points to the medicine, the clinic, or the school, never to the doctor alone.
normalIntro.cn: veterinary 是形容词：它总是指向「药物、诊所、学校」，而不是单独指医生本人。

normal.en: The noun for the person is veterinarian, or the short vet.
normal.cn: 指人的名词是 veterinarian，或缩略的 vet。

normal.en: Veterinary medicine is both the science and the medicine itself.
normal.cn: veterinary medicine 既可指兽医学，也可指兽药本身。

normal.en: British speech uses veterinary surgeon and clips it to the vet.
normal.cn: 英式说法用 veterinary surgeon，并把它缩略为 vet。

normal.en: The Latin source kept beasts of burden, so veterinary stays tied to farm animals as well as pets.
normal.cn: 拉丁来源保留了「驮畜」的意思，所以 veterinary 既关联宠物，也关联农场牲畜。

normal.en: Do not confuse veterinary with veteran, even though the openings look alike.
normal.cn: 尽管开头相似，不要把 veterinary 与 veteran 混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a chart of a cow on a clinic wall with the word veterinary across the top.
abstract.cn: 想象诊所墙上贴着一张牛的解剖图，顶部写着 veterinary。

abstract.en: See a stethoscope resting beside a horseshoe on a white table.
abstract.cn: 想象白色台面上，听诊器放在一块马蹄铁旁边。

abstract.en: Think of two doors in a hospital: one for people, one marked veterinary.
abstract.cn: 想象医院里有两扇门，一扇给人，一扇标着 veterinary。

examples.en: He is studying veterinary science at university.
examples.cn: 他在大学攻读兽医学。

examples.en: The team opened a new veterinary clinic in the village.
examples.cn: 团队在村里开了一家新的动物诊所。

examples.en: Veterinary costs for large animals can be very high.
examples.cn: 大型牲畜的兽医费用可能非常高。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂特 ə ri」——专门「喂」养「特」别的动物、给它们看病的，就是兽医这一行；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 veterina（驮畜）+ -arius（属于……的）→ veterinarius（驮畜的）→ 英语 veterinary，核心义「与牲畜医疗相关」。更早的词根可能与 vetus（年老的）相关，但来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Veterinary begins as an adjective for animal care, widens to the whole field of animal medicine, and in British use also names the animal doctor.
sensesIntro.cn: veterinary 起初是表示动物照料的形容词，扩展到整个动物医学领域，英式用法中还兼指兽医本人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clinic wall of animal charts and medical tools.
core.cn: 核心意象：挂满动物图谱与医疗器械的诊所墙面。

branches.en: The adjective for animal care is the base sense.
branches.cn: 表示动物照料的形容词是基础义项。

branches.en: The field of study grows from the adjective plus science.
branches.cn: 学科义项由该形容词与 science 等词的固定搭配生长而来。

branches.en: The British noun use clips the title to the person.
branches.cn: 英式名词用法把这一头衔缩略后指人。

branches.en: Clinical care and academic study share the same word.
branches.cn: 临床护理与学术研究共用同一个词。

branches.en: The adjective and the British noun both point to the same animal doctor.
branches.cn: 形容词与英式名词都指向同一位兽医。

intro.en: Veterinary is Latin veterinarius reshaped by the English suffix -ary, linked to veterinarian and vet.
intro.cn: veterinary 是拉丁语 veterinarius 经英语词尾 -ary 改造的结果，与 veterinarian、vet 相联系。

latinIntro.en: Latin veterina means beasts of burden, and veterinarius means belonging to them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 veterina 意为驮畜，veterinarius 意为属于驮畜的。

items.example: Veterina is the base noun behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: veterina 是整个词族的基干名词。

items.example: Veterinarius is reshaped into the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: veterinarius 被改造成英语形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ary makes veterinary an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 使 veterinary 成为形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ian forms veterinarian from the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ian 由该形容词构成 veterinarian。

items.example: The doctor for animals is the veterinarian.
items.exampleCN: 给动物看病的医生是 veterinarian。

items.meaning: the science and practice of healing
items.example: Veterinary medicine is the field of animal healing.
items.exampleCN: veterinary medicine 指动物医疗这一领域。

items.example: Veterinary surgeon is the older British title.
items.exampleCN: veterinary surgeon 是更早的英式头衔。

items.meaning: organised knowledge of the natural world
items.example: Veterinary science names the academic field.
items.exampleCN: veterinary science 指这一学术领域。

items.meaning: a place where patients are treated
items.example: A veterinary clinic treats animals rather than people.
items.exampleCN: veterinary clinic 治疗的是动物而不是人。

definition_zh: 否决；否决权；行使否决权阻止
definition_en: to stop a proposal or decision with the right to refuse it, or the formal power to do so
core_image: 一只手把刚递上来的文件按回桌面，在旁边写下「不准」
scene: 部长在会议最后把手按在文件上。The minister raised his hand and vetoed the proposal.
sceneCN: 这里 veto 是「否决；行使否决权」（第 1 个义项：用正式权力拒绝提案）；句意：部长举起手，否决了这项提案。

derivatives.zh: veto 加 -ing 构成的形容词，表示「正在行使否决的」
veto 加 -er 构成，指行使否决的人或机构，属较少见用法
veto 加 -less 构成，表示「没有否决权的」，多见于政治评论

senses.title: To reject a proposal with official power
senses.definition: to use formal authority to refuse a proposal, bill, or plan
senses.definitionCN: 用正式权力拒绝提案、法案或计划
senses.example: The president vetoed the bill on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 总统在周五否决了这项法案。
senses.why: The Latin phrase behind the word means I forbid, so the act starts as a single blocking word.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁语句子意为「我禁止」，因此这个动作最初就是一个拦阻的词。

senses.title: The right to refuse
senses.definition: the legal or official power to stop a proposal or decision
senses.definitionCN: 阻止提案或决定的法定或正式权力
senses.example: The committee has a veto over the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 该委员会对预算拥有否决权。
senses.why: The blocking word becomes the name of the power that does the blocking.
senses.whyCN: 那个拦阻的词后来直接成为实施拦阻的权力本身的名称。

senses.title: A formal refusal
senses.definition: an official refusal that prevents something from going ahead
senses.definitionCN: 阻止某事继续推进的正式拒绝
senses.example: Her veto ended months of planning.
senses.exampleCN: 她的否决结束了数月的筹划。
senses.why: The action of blocking is turned into a countable event, a refusal on record.
senses.whyCN: 拦下的动作被转成可数的事件，即记录在案的一次拒绝。

senses.title: The international political privilege
senses.definition: the right of certain states to stop a decision inside a global body
senses.definitionCN: 某些国家在全球机构内部阻止决定的特权
senses.example: Only a few nations hold that veto.
senses.exampleCN: 只有少数国家掌握这项否决权。
senses.why: The old Roman word now names a modern diplomatic privilege.
senses.whyCN: 古罗马的旧词如今命名一种现代外交特权。

senses.title: An everyday informal block
senses.titleCN: 日常口语中的一票拦下
senses.definition: an informal refusal by one person that stops a group plan
senses.definitionCN: 一个人临时拒绝而使集体计划停下
senses.example: Dad put a veto on the late night trip.
senses.exampleCN: 爸爸否掉了这次深夜出行。
senses.why: The heavy formal word is borrowed for playful family decisions.
senses.whyCN: 这个庄重的正式词被借来处理家庭里的决定，带点玩笑意味。

senses.title: A stop signal in animal training
senses.titleCN: 动物训练中的制止信号
senses.definition: a learned cue that tells another animal to stop its action
senses.definitionCN: 训练出来的、让另一只动物停止动作的信号
senses.example: The trainer taught the dog a simple veto.
senses.exampleCN: 训练员教会那只狗一个简单的制止信号。
senses.why: The idea of saying no is extended to animals that are taught to stop.
senses.whyCN: 「说不」的概念被扩展到被教会停下来听指令的动物身上。

senses.title: Refusal of a card payment
senses.definition: a refusal by a bank or card issuer to authorise a payment
senses.definitionCN: 银行或发卡机构拒绝授权某笔支付
senses.example: The shop was told the payment had a veto.
senses.exampleCN: 商店被告知这笔付款被拒付。
senses.why: A silent system now plays the role of the one who forbids the transaction.
senses.whyCN: 如今一个沉默的系统扮演了禁止交易的那个角色。

senses.title: A moral objection
senses.definition: a personal declaration that rules out an option for ethical reasons
senses.definitionCN: 因道德理由而宣布某个选项不可行
senses.example: She used her veto on animal testing.
senses.exampleCN: 她对使用动物实验行使了自己的否决。
senses.why: The power to refuse moves from law into personal conscience.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝的权力从法律领域移动到个人良知之中。

intro.en: Veto is Latin for I forbid, the first word of the formula a Roman tribune used to block a law.
intro.cn: veto 是拉丁语「我禁止」，本是古罗马保民官拦阻法律时那句定式的第一个词。

items.en: Veto is the first person singular of vetare, to forbid.
items.cn: veto 是 vetare（禁止）的第一人称单数形式。

items.en: A tribune spoke this one word between a law and its passage.
items.cn: 保民官在法律与通过之间说出这一个词。

items.en: English adopts the word for a refusal of assent.
items.cn: 英语借用该词表示拒不同意。

items.en: Treaty and UN language turns it into a named power.
items.cn: 条约与联合国用语把它变成一种有名称的权力。

items.en: Everyday speech extends it to family and social decisions.
items.cn: 现代口语把它延伸到家庭与社会决定。

note.en: Veto sits with same-root Latin forbidding words on one side and general refusal words on the other.
note.cn: veto 一边连着同源的拉丁语「禁止」词，一边连着普通的「拒绝」词。

entries.definition: Latin verb meaning to forbid
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语动词「禁止」，是 veto 的词根

entries.definition: the past form of veto, meaning refused
entries.definitionCN: veto 的过去式，表示「被否决了」

entries.definition: a devoted follower
entries.definitionCN: 信徒；追随者；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to refuse to accept something
to set aside a decision by higher authority
to forbid something officially

normalIntro.en: Veto is one word that stops a motion: the Latin speaker says I forbid and the proposal falls.
normalIntro.cn: veto 就是一个能叫停动议的词：拉丁语使用者说「我禁止」，提案就应声倒下。

normal.en: To veto a bill is to stop it from becoming law.
normal.cn: veto a bill 就是阻止法案成为法律。

normal.en: Veto power is the right to say no formally.
normal.cn: veto power 就是正式说「不行」的权利。

normal.en: A presidential veto can often be overridden by a vote.
normal.cn: 总统否决常常可以被投票推翻。

normal.en: To exercise the veto means to use that power once.
normal.cn: exercise the veto 就是动用一次这项权力。

normal.en: Latin vetare means to forbid, so veto is a forbidding word.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 vetare 意为禁止，因此 veto 本身就是「禁止」之词。

abstract.en: A red stamp lands on a page and the whole plan stops.
abstract.cn: 一枚红章落在纸面，整个计划就此停住。

abstract.en: One raised hand in a full room cancels the vote.
abstract.cn: 满场之中一只手举起，表决便被取消。

abstract.en: A gate that only swings shut: the formal word closes the road.
abstract.cn: 一扇只会关上的闸门：这个正式的词把路封住。

examples.en: The council vetoed the plan to build a car park.
examples.cn: 委员会否决了修建停车场的计划。

examples.en: A single member can exercise the veto in this club.
examples.cn: 在这个俱乐部里，任何一名成员都可以行使否决权。

examples.en: The mayor has a veto over the annual budget.
examples.cn: 市长对年度预算拥有否决权。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维托」——会议上的维托先生一举手，提案就被否决；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vetare（禁止）→ veto（我禁止）→ 古罗马保民官的拦阻词 → 英语 veto，核心义「以权力叫停」。

sensesIntro.en: Veto starts as the formal act of refusal, then becomes the power itself, then the recorded refusal, and finally spreads to politics, family talk, animals, and money.
sensesIntro.cn: veto 先指正式的拒绝动作，再指这种权力本身，接着指一次记录在案的拒绝，最后扩展到政治、家庭口语、动物训练与支付领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand that stops a document from passing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只举起的手，让文件停在通过之前。

branches.en: The act of refusing a proposal is the main verb sense.
branches.cn: 拒绝提案的动作是主要的动词义项。

branches.en: The power behind the act becomes a noun of its own.
branches.cn: 动作背后的权力单独成为名词义项。

branches.en: The refusal itself is counted as a single event.
branches.cn: 拒绝本身被计作一次独立的事件。

branches.en: In world politics the same power belongs to states.
branches.cn: 在世界政治中，同一权力归属于国家。

branches.en: Borrowed informally, the same word covers family plans and moral stands.
branches.cn: 非正式借用时，同一个词可指家庭计划与道德立场。

intro.en: Veto is a bare Latin word rather than a prefix plus root, so its forms grow by English endings.
intro.cn: veto 是整块借来的拉丁语词，不是前缀加词根，因此其形式靠英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family of vetare supplies the forbidding core and later English nouns.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vetare 一族提供了「禁止」的核心，也提供了后来的英语名词。

items.example: Latin lawmakers could vetare a motion.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语中的立法者可以禁止一项动议。

items.example: The single ending creates the phrase veto.
items.exampleCN: 这个单个词尾构成了短语 veto。

items.meaningCN: 过去式或过去分词词尾
items.example: The suffix forms vetoed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 vetoed。

items.meaning: more than one, used after o
items.meaningCN: 复数词尾，接在以 o 结尾的词后
items.example: The suffix forms vetoes.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -es 构成 vetoes。

items.example: The suffix forms vetoing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 vetoing。

items.example: The suffix forms vetoer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 vetoer。

items.example: The suffix forms vetoless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 vetoless。

items.example: The prefix forms override, as in override a veto.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 构成 override，如推翻否决。

items.example: The prefix forms anti-veto groups.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 anti- 构成反否决团体。

latinEntries.meaning: to forbid, to forbid by law
